[§](https://docs.rs#using-egui)Using egui

To see what is possible to build with egui you can check out the online demo at [https://www.egui.rs/#demo](https://www.egui.rs/#demo).

If you like the “learning by doing” approach, clone [https://github.com/emilk/eframe_template](https://github.com/emilk/eframe_template) and get started using egui right away.

[§](https://docs.rs#a-simple-example)A simple example

Here is a simple counter that can be incremented and decremented using two buttons:

```
fn ui_counter(ui: &mut egui::Ui, counter: &mut i32) {
    // Put the buttons and label on the same row:
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        if ui.button("−").clicked() {
            *counter -= 1;
        }
        ui.label(counter.to_string());
        if ui.button("+").clicked() {
            *counter += 1;
        }
    });
}
```
In some GUI frameworks this would require defining multiple types and functions with callbacks or message handlers,
but thanks to `egui` being immediate mode everything is one self-contained function!

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick start

```
ui.label("This is a label");
ui.hyperlink("https://github.com/emilk/egui");
ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut my_string);
if ui.button("Click me").clicked() { }
ui.add(egui::Slider::new(&mut my_f32, 0.0..=100.0));
ui.add(egui::DragValue::new(&mut my_f32));
ui.checkbox(&mut my_boolean, "Checkbox");
#[derive(PartialEq)]
enum Enum { First, Second, Third }
ui.horizontal(|ui| {
    ui.radio_value(&mut my_enum, Enum::First, "First");
    ui.radio_value(&mut my_enum, Enum::Second, "Second");
    ui.radio_value(&mut my_enum, Enum::Third, "Third");
});
ui.separator();
ui.image((my_image, egui::Vec2::new(640.0, 480.0)));
ui.collapsing("Click to see what is hidden!", |ui| {
    ui.label("Not much, as it turns out");
});
```
[§](https://docs.rs#viewports)Viewports

Some egui backends support multiple *viewports*, which is what egui calls the native OS windows it resides in.
See [ crate::viewport](https://docs.rs/viewport/index.html) for more information.

[§](https://docs.rs#coordinate-system)Coordinate system

The left-top corner of the screen is `(0.0, 0.0)`,
with X increasing to the right and Y increasing downwards.

`egui` uses logical *points* as its coordinate system.
Those related to physical *pixels* by the `pixels_per_point` scale factor.
For example, a high-dpi screen can have `pixels_per_point = 2.0`,
meaning there are two physical screen pixels for each logical point.

Angles are in radians, and are measured clockwise from the X-axis, which has angle=0.

[§](https://docs.rs#integrating-with-egui)Integrating with egui

Most likely you are using an existing `egui` backend/integration such as [ eframe](https://docs.rs/eframe),

[, or](https://docs.rs/bevy_egui)

`bevy_egui`[, but if you want to integrate](https://github.com/not-fl3/egui-miniquad)

`egui-miniquad``egui` into a new game engine or graphics backend, this is the section for you.You need to collect [ RawInput](https://docs.rs/struct.RawInput.html) and handle

[. The basic structure is this:](https://docs.rs/struct.FullOutput.html)

`FullOutput````
let mut ctx = egui::Context::default();
// Game loop:
loop {
    let raw_input: egui::RawInput = gather_input();
    let full_output = ctx.run(raw_input, |ctx| {
        egui::CentralPanel::default().show(&ctx, |ui| {
            ui.label("Hello world!");
            if ui.button("Click me").clicked() {
                // take some action here
            }
        });
    });
    handle_platform_output(full_output.platform_output);
    let clipped_primitives = ctx.tessellate(full_output.shapes, full_output.pixels_per_point);
    paint(full_output.textures_delta, clipped_primitives);
}
```
For a reference OpenGL renderer, see [the  egui_glow painter](https://github.com/emilk/egui/blob/main/crates/egui_glow/src/painter.rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#debugging-your-renderer)Debugging your renderer

[§](https://docs.rs#things-look-jagged)Things look jagged

- Turn off backface culling.

[§](https://docs.rs#my-text-is-blurry)My text is blurry

- Make sure you set the proper `pixels_per_point`in the input to egui.
- Make sure the texture sampler is not off by half a pixel. Try nearest-neighbor sampler to check.

[§](https://docs.rs#my-windows-are-too-transparent-or-too-dark)My windows are too transparent or too dark

- egui uses premultiplied alpha, so make sure your blending function is `(ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)`.
- Make sure your texture sampler is clamped (`GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE`).
- egui prefers gamma color spaces for all blending so:
- Do NOT use an sRGBA-aware texture (NOT `GL_SRGB8_ALPHA8`).
- Multiply texture and vertex colors in gamma space
- Turn OFF sRGBA/gamma framebuffer (NO `GL_FRAMEBUFFER_SRGB`).

- Do NOT use an sRGBA-aware texture (NOT

[§](https://docs.rs#understanding-immediate-mode)Understanding immediate mode

`egui` is an immediate mode GUI library.

Immediate mode has its roots in gaming, where everything on the screen is painted at the display refresh rate, i.e. at 60+ frames per second. In immediate mode GUIs, the entire interface is laid out and painted at the same high rate. This makes immediate mode GUIs especially well suited for highly interactive applications.

It is useful to fully grok what “immediate mode” implies.

Here is an example to illustrate it:

```
if ui.button("click me").clicked() {
    take_action()
}
```
This code is being executed each frame at maybe 60 frames per second. Each frame egui does these things:

- lays out the letters `click me`in order to figure out the size of the button
- decides where on screen to place the button
- check if the mouse is hovering or clicking that location
- choose button colors based on if it is being hovered or clicked
- add a `Shape::Rect``Shape::Text`
- return a `Response``clicked`

There is no button being created and stored somewhere.
The only output of this call is some colored shapes, and a [ Response](https://docs.rs/response/struct.Response.html).

Similarly, consider this code:

`ui.add(egui::Slider::new(&mut value, 0.0..=100.0).text("My value"));`Here egui will read `value` (an `f32`) to display the slider, then look if the mouse is dragging the slider and if so change the `value`.
Note that `egui` does not store the slider value for you - it only displays the current value, and changes it
by how much the slider has been dragged in the previous few milliseconds.
This means it is responsibility of the egui user to store the state (`value`) so that it persists between frames.

It can be useful to read the code for the toggle switch example widget to get a better understanding
of how egui works: [https://github.com/emilk/egui/blob/main/crates/egui_demo_lib/src/demo/toggle_switch.rs](https://github.com/emilk/egui/blob/main/crates/egui_demo_lib/src/demo/toggle_switch.rs).

Read more about the pros and cons of immediate mode at [https://github.com/emilk/egui#why-immediate-mode](https://github.com/emilk/egui#why-immediate-mode).

[§](https://docs.rs#multi-pass-immediate-mode)Multi-pass immediate mode

By default, egui usually only does one pass for each rendered frame.
However, egui supports multi-pass immediate mode.
Another pass can be requested with [ Context::request_discard](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html#method.request_discard).

This is used by some widgets to cover up “first-frame jitters”.
For instance, the [ Grid](https://docs.rs/struct.Grid.html) needs to know the width of all columns before it can properly place the widgets.
But it cannot know the width of widgets to come.
So it stores the max widths of previous frames and uses that.
This means the first time a

`Grid` is shown it will *guess*the widths of the columns, and will usually guess wrong. This means the contents of the grid will be wrong for one frame, before settling to the correct places. Therefore

`Grid` calls [when it is first shown, so the wrong placement is never visible to the end user.](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html#method.request_discard)

`Context::request_discard`This is an example of a form of multi-pass immediate mode, where earlier passes are used for sizing, and later passes for layout.

See [ Context::request_discard](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html#method.request_discard) and

[for more.](https://docs.rs/struct.Options.html#structfield.max_passes)

`Options::max_passes`[§](https://docs.rs#misc)Misc

[§](https://docs.rs#how-widgets-works)How widgets works

`if ui.button("click me").clicked() { take_action() }`is short for

```
let button = egui::Button::new("click me");
if ui.add(button).clicked() { take_action() }
```
which is short for

```
let button = egui::Button::new("click me");
let response = button.ui(ui);
if response.clicked() { take_action() }
```
[ Button](https://docs.rs/widgets/struct.Button.html) uses the builder pattern to create the data required to show it. The

[is then discarded.](https://docs.rs/widgets/struct.Button.html)

`Button`[ Button](https://docs.rs/widgets/struct.Button.html) implements

`trait` [, which looks like this:](https://docs.rs/widgets/trait.Widget.html)

`Widget````
pub trait Widget {
    /// Allocate space, interact, paint, and return a [`Response`].
    fn ui(self, ui: &mut Ui) -> Response;
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#widget-interaction)Widget interaction

Each widget has a [ Sense](https://docs.rs/struct.Sense.html), which defines whether or not the widget
is sensitive to clicking and/or drags.

For instance, a [ Button](https://docs.rs/widgets/struct.Button.html) only has a

[(by default). This means if you drag a button it will not respond with](https://docs.rs/struct.Sense.html#method.click)

`Sense::click`[. Instead, the drag will continue through the button to the first widget behind it that is sensitive to dragging, which for instance could be a](https://docs.rs/response/struct.Response.html#method.dragged)

`Response::dragged`[. This lets you scroll by dragging a scroll area (important on touch screens), just as long as you don’t drag on a widget that is sensitive to drags (e.g. a](https://docs.rs/containers/scroll_area/struct.ScrollArea.html)

`ScrollArea`[).](https://docs.rs/widgets/struct.Slider.html)

`Slider`When widgets overlap it is the last added one that is considered to be on top and which will get input priority.

The widget interaction logic is run at the *start* of each frame,
based on the output from the previous frame.
This means that when a new widget shows up you cannot click it in the same
frame (i.e. in the same fraction of a second), but unless the user
is spider-man, they wouldn’t be fast enough to do so anyways.

By running the interaction code early, egui can actually
tell you if a widget is being interacted with *before* you add it,
as long as you know its [ Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html) before-hand (e.g. using

[), by calling](https://docs.rs/struct.Ui.html#method.next_auto_id)

`Ui::next_auto_id`[. This can be useful in some circumstances in order to style a widget, or to respond to interactions before adding the widget (perhaps on top of other widgets).](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html#method.read_response)

`Context::read_response`[§](https://docs.rs#auto-sizing-panels-and-windows)Auto-sizing panels and windows

In egui, all panels and windows auto-shrink to fit the content. If the window or panel is also resizable, this can lead to a weird behavior where you can drag the edge of the panel/window to make it larger, and when you release the panel/window shrinks again. This is an artifact of immediate mode, and here are some alternatives on how to avoid it:

- Turn off resizing with `Window::resizable``Panel::resizable`
- Wrap your panel contents in a `ScrollArea``Window::vscroll``Window::hscroll`
- Use a justified layout:

```
ui.with_layout(egui::Layout::top_down_justified(egui::Align::Center), |ui| {
    ui.button("I am becoming wider as needed");
});
```
- Fill in extra space with emptiness:

`ui.allocate_space(ui.available_size()); // put this LAST in your panel/window code`[§](https://docs.rs#sizes)Sizes

You can control the size of widgets using [ Ui::add_sized](https://docs.rs/struct.Ui.html#method.add_sized).

`ui.add_sized([40.0, 20.0], egui::DragValue::new(&mut my_value));`[§](https://docs.rs#code-snippets)Code snippets

```
// Miscellaneous tips and tricks
ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
    ui.spacing_mut().item_spacing.x = 0.0; // remove spacing between widgets
    // `radio_value` also works for enums, integers, and more.
    ui.radio_value(&mut some_bool, false, "Off");
    ui.radio_value(&mut some_bool, true, "On");
});
ui.group(|ui| {
    ui.label("Within a frame");
    ui.set_min_height(200.0);
});
// A `scope` creates a temporary [`Ui`] in which you can change settings:
ui.scope(|ui| {
    ui.visuals_mut().override_text_color = Some(egui::Color32::RED);
    ui.style_mut().override_text_style = Some(egui::TextStyle::Monospace);
    ui.style_mut().wrap_mode = Some(TextWrapMode::Truncate);
    ui.label("This text will be red, monospace, and won't wrap to a new line");
}); // the temporary settings are reverted here
```
[§](https://docs.rs#installing-additional-fonts)Installing additional fonts

The default egui fonts only support latin and cryllic characters, and some emojis.
To use egui with e.g. asian characters you need to install your own font (`.ttf` or `.otf`) using [ Context::set_fonts](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html#method.set_fonts).

[§](https://docs.rs#instrumentation)Instrumentation

This crate supports using the [profiling](https://crates.io/crates/profiling) crate for instrumentation.
You can enable features on the profiling crates in your application to add instrumentation for all
crates that support it, including egui. See the profiling crate docs for more information.

```
[dependencies]
profiling = "1.0"
[features]
profile-with-puffin = ["profiling/profile-with-puffin"]
```
[§](https://docs.rs#custom-allocator)Custom allocator

egui apps can run significantly (~20%) faster by using a custom allocator, like [mimalloc](https://crates.io/crates/mimalloc) or [talc](https://crates.io/crates/talc).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [cache](https://docs.rs/cache/index.html)
- Caches for preventing the same value from being recomputed every frame.
- [containers](https://docs.rs/containers/index.html)
- Containers are pieces of the UI which wraps other pieces of UI. Examples: `Window``ScrollArea``Resize``Panel`
- [debug_](https://docs.rs/debug_text/index.html)- text
- This is an example of how to create a plugin for egui.
- [gui_](https://docs.rs/gui_zoom/index.html)- zoom
- Helpers for zooming the whole GUI of an app (changing `Context::pixels_per_point`
- [introspection](https://docs.rs/introspection/index.html)
- Showing UI:s for egui/epaint types.

# facett_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-core/^0.1/

## Expand description

**facett-core** — the visual kernel. Render a node/edge ** Scene** into egui.
Source-agnostic: build a

`Scene` from anything (Arrow rows, a graph, a DAG),
hand it here, get pixels. The CPU painter is the reference; a **wgpu**fast path (GPU viewport-cull + indirect draw, seeded from katana-osm’s

`osm-viewer`) lands behind this same `draw()` call — consumers don’t change.## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use a11y::`- [Semantics](https://docs.rs/a11y/struct.Semantics.html);
- `pub use a11y::`- [node](https://docs.rs/a11y/fn.node.html)as a11y_node;
- `pub use a11y::`- [stable_id](https://docs.rs/a11y/fn.stable_id.html);
- `pub use caps::`- [FacetCaps](https://docs.rs/caps/struct.FacetCaps.html);
- `pub use clip::`- [ArrowColumnRef](https://docs.rs/clip/struct.ArrowColumnRef.html);
- `pub use clip::`- [ClipKind](https://docs.rs/clip/enum.ClipKind.html);
- `pub use clip::`- [ClipPayload](https://docs.rs/clip/enum.ClipPayload.html);
- `pub use clip::`- [CopySource](https://docs.rs/clip/trait.CopySource.html);
- `pub use clip::`- [PasteTarget](https://docs.rs/clip/trait.PasteTarget.html);
- `pub use clipboard::`- [ClipAction](https://docs.rs/clipboard/enum.ClipAction.html);
- `pub use deckfx::`- [DeckFx](https://docs.rs/deckfx/struct.DeckFx.html);
- `pub use deckfx::`- [DeckRaven](https://docs.rs/deckfx/struct.DeckRaven.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [a11y](https://docs.rs/a11y/index.html)
- **facett-core::a11y**— the FC-4 enabler. One helper that makes a- *custom-painted*element appear in the AccessKit tree.
- [caps](https://docs.rs/caps/index.html)
- **Uniform capability model**— every- `Facet`- `FacetCaps`- `FacetDeck`- `.nornir/design/capability-model.md`.
- [chrome](https://docs.rs/chrome/index.html)
- **chrome**— the shared- **glass / card**decoration (Tier-1 §T1.3): a rounded frame with an- `effects::glow_rect`- `overlay::glass_tint`- `EffectsPolicy`- `Full`/- `Reduced`, a crisp opaque panel under- `None`/Device.
- [clip](https://docs.rs/clip/index.html)
- **Cross-facet typed copy/paste**(§16) — the trait + payload machinery so copy/paste carries- **full typed data**between facett components, not just text. A process-wide transfer registry holds the last typed- `ClipPayload`
- [clipboard](https://docs.rs/clipboard/index.html)
- **Uniform clipboard**— cut / copy / paste routed the same way for every- `Facet`- *gesture*as semantic events (- `egui::Event::Copy`- `Cut`- `Paste`- `TextEdit`consumes first — so a form field handles its own copy and the facet-level- `copy`- `poll`- `put`- `copy`/- `cut`- *return*the text). See- `.nornir/design/clipboard.md`.
- [deckfx](https://docs.rs/deckfx/index.html)
- **Deck-level effects + theming**— wires the- `theme`- `effects`- `FacetDeck`- **opt-in, host-controllable**features.
- [edges](https://docs.rs/edges/index.html)
- **Graph edge rendering**(§18) — straight, spline (cubic Bézier / Catmull-Rom sampled), and fat/soft (variable width, feathered) edges, with widths/softness from the theme.- **Device**= crisp hairlines, no glow (gated by- `EffectsPolicy`
- [effects](https://docs.rs/effects/index.html)
- **effects**— motion + bloom for the facett look. Pure egui,- **glow backend only**: everything here paints with layered alpha shapes on an- `egui::Painter`
- [focus](https://docs.rs/focus/index.html)
- **Focus hints, pane revolver, and form groups**(§13 FOC-3/FOC-4 + FORM-*). All off-by-default, themed, and- **deterministic**(no ambient time): the hint labels are a pure function of the focusables; the revolver transform is a pure function of- `(progress, target, viewport)`; form navigation is pure rect geometry reusing- `nav::nearest_in_direction`- `Memory::request_focus`/- `move_focus`) at the call site.
- [harness](https://docs.rs/harness/index.html)
- Headless test harness — **fire up a**: its`Facet`, inject data, render it offscreen, and capture what it drew`state_json`+ a vertex count (a “it drew something” proxy) + a stderr activity trail. No display, no GPU. This is the basis of facett’s auto test matrix, and mirrors nornir viz’s`NORNIR_VIZ_STATE`introspection — every component is observable from outside.
- [imgscan](https://docs.rs/imgscan/index.html)
- **imgscan**— the reusable IMAGE-ANALYSIS oracle (SCAN-THE-PIXELS law).
- [labels3d](https://docs.rs/labels3d/index.html)
- **3D label “gyro” stabilization**(§19) — fix labels bobbing while the scene rotates. The label’s 3D anchor is projected to- **screen space**, then the text is drawn- **billboarded**(upright, camera-facing) — never rotated with the scene (GYRO-1). Vertical jitter is eliminated by- **stable sub-pixel placement**(consistent rounding) + optional- **temporal smoothing**of the projected anchor (GYRO-2). The galley is cached once per label by the caller (no per-frame relayout).
- [look](https://docs.rs/look/index.html)
- **facett look & feel**(the work-order architecture, §3) — one- `Theme`- **Windows**,- **macOS**,- **Device**(effects-off, rugged/military). The- `Theme`- *single source of truth*:- `Theme::apply`- `egui::Style`(visuals + spacing + scroll) plus the text scale in one call, and also publishes the derived legacy- `crate::Theme`
- [nav](https://docs.rs/nav/index.html)
- **Shared spatial navigation + focus**(§13 FOC-2, §14 NAV-1) — the- *one*pan/zoom model (- `Navigable`) reused by map/graph/plot/canvas, and the- *one*spatial focus rule (- `nearest_in_direction`) reused by pane and form navigation (COH-3). Pan/zoom is expressed as an- `egui::emath::TSTransform`(scale + offset), so a host can also use it to transform an overlaid guest layer (§5 CMP-4).
- [overlay](https://docs.rs/overlay/index.html)
- **Composability & overlays**(§5) +- **glass / masks**(§20) — render any facett component into an arbitrary sub-- `Rect`/layer of any other (a dataframe pinned over a map, a HUD over video), clipped by a- **mask**, with optional glass gated by- `EffectsPolicy`
- [rabbit](https://docs.rs/rabbit/index.html)
- **The znippy rabbit**— facett’s synthetic/test mascot, as reusable- *parametric*geometry. znippy ships no logo asset, so the rabbit is generated here: a friendly sitting-rabbit silhouette (rounded body + head + two upright ears + an eye dot), built from deterministic arcs in a normalised- `[-1, 1]²`design box (x right, y- **up**). No RNG, no per-frame randomness — two calls produce byte-identical geometry, so the wgpu/CPU snapshots stay stable.
- [render](https://docs.rs/render/index.html)
- The L0 shared render kernel (CONS-CORE) — shared `Camera`, z-ordered`LayerStack`, the CPU rect scissor, and (feature`wgpu`) the extracted GPU scaffold. Map skins +`facett-graphview`draw through this.`facett-core::render``facett-graphview`draw through (the CONS-CORE seam).
- [runtrace](https://docs.rs/runtrace/index.html)
- **In-memory render/exec trace**— the wasm-safe “what actually RAN” ledger.
- [scroll_](https://docs.rs/scroll_engine/index.html)- engine
- **CygnusEd smooth-scroll engine**(§11) — pixel-by-pixel, sub-pixel soft scrolling with momentum/acceleration, à la the Amiga editor’s jerkyless feel. The scroll- *offset*is decoupled from row height (renderers paint at a- **fractional**pixel offset + clip), and the whole thing is- **deterministic under an injected clock**(- `advance(dt)`), so snapshots reproduce exactly (FC-7 / P0-5). Reusable by text, console, and the dataframe grid (SCRL-3).
- [testmatrix](https://docs.rs/testmatrix/index.html)
- **The functional-status → nornir test-matrix bridge**(feature- `testmatrix`).
- [theme](https://docs.rs/theme/index.html)
- **Theming.**A palette the custom-painted components (graph/depgraph/map) read from the egui context, plus matching egui- `Visuals`for the standard widgets (pop/table/pipeline). Call- `set_theme`- `Theme::default`- `Theme::sci_fi`- `Theme::nordic_aurora`- `Theme::cyberpunk_neon`- `Theme::amber_crt`- `Theme::deep_space`- `Theme::hugin_noir`- `Theme::ALL`- `Theme::by_name`
- [trace](https://docs.rs/trace/index.html)
- Structured event trace — the **machine-readable**sibling of`harness::trail`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Edge](https://docs.rs/struct.Edge.html)
- A directed edge between node indices.
- [Facet](https://docs.rs/struct.FacetDeck.html)- Deck
- A tabbed set of `Facet`**every**facet’s`state_json`under its title, so the whole-app introspection contract is free. korp/nornir can build their window from a`FacetDeck`instead of hand-rolling tabs + the state dump.
- [Node](https://docs.rs/struct.Node.html)
- A node: a label + a colour (the *consumer*picks the colour policy — hash by label, by status, …).
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.Scene.html)
- A drawable graph: nodes + edges (edges index into `nodes`).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Layout](https://docs.rs/enum.Layout.html)
- Node placement strategy.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Facet](https://docs.rs/trait.Facet.html)
- The facett **component contract**. Every facet — graph, map, pipeline, table, the ported nornir viewers — implements this, so consumers (korp, nornir, …) compose them uniformly*and*get headless robot-testing for free.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [draw](https://docs.rs/fn.draw.html)
- Draw a `Scene`into`ui`— the reusable render primitive. Empty scenes show`empty_hint`. Labels render when the node count is small enough to read.
- [hash_](https://docs.rs/fn.hash_color.html)- color
- A stable, bright-ish colour from a string (FNV-1a). Handy default node colour.
- [layout_](https://docs.rs/fn.layout_positions.html)- positions
- **Test/host hook (additive).**The public, return-asserted view of the private [- `positions`] layout node — the exact node centres- `draw`- `scene`under- `layout`inside- `rect`. Exposed so the graph-skin call-chain matrix can assert the- *layout*stage (finite, in-rect, count == nodes, circular radius, force-fit normalisation) without a painter. Calls the- **same**private fn- `draw`uses, so it IS the layout the pixels come from — additive, no behaviour change.

# facett_video - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/facett-video/0.1.10/target-redirect/facett_video/

## Expand description

**facett-video** (§22) — a video player whose chrome (transport, play/pause,
scrubber, volume, time, fullscreen) is **themed** and driven by the shared
[ KeyMap](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/look/keymap/struct.KeyMap.html); decode is a

**pluggable backend**trait (

[). M2 ships the](https://docs.rs/trait.FrameSource.html)

`FrameSource`[frame-source backend (a consumer pushes RGBA frames → texture each frame →](https://docs.rs/struct.FrameSequence.html)

`FrameSequence``ui.image`) for image
sequences / sim / camera (VID-2). The optional `egui-video` FFmpeg backend is
a host-side feature (VID-1).Overlay-ready (annotations/HUD via §5); **ROI selection** like the grid’s
range select (VID-3). **Copy a frame** yields a typed
[ ClipPayload::Image](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/clip/enum.ClipPayload.html) (the M2 image-copy
Exit criterion).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Frame](https://docs.rs/struct.FrameSequence.html)- Sequence
- The frame-source backend (VID-2): an in-memory RGBA image sequence a consumer pushes into. Deterministic → the player snapshots + tests headlessly.
- [Video](https://docs.rs/struct.VideoPlayer.html)- Player
- The video player. Owns transport state + position + ROI; the decode is a boxed
`FrameSource`**injected clock**(`advance(dt)`), so it is deterministic for snapshots.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Frame](https://docs.rs/trait.FrameSource.html)- Source
- A pluggable decode backend (VID-1): hands the player the current frame as an
egui `egui::ColorImage`

[134](#134)    pub fn advance(&mut self, dt: f32) {
[136](#136)        if !self.playing || self.source.frame_count() == 0 {
[137](#137)            return;
[138](#138)        }
[139](#139)        self.accum += dt * self.source.fps();
[140](#140)        while self.accum >= 1.0 {
[141](#141)            self.accum -= 1.0;
[142](#142)            self.frame = (self.frame + 1) % self.source.frame_count();
[143](#143)        }
[144](#144)    }

# KeyMap in facett_core::look::keymap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/look/keymap/struct.KeyMap.html

```
pub struct KeyMap {
    pub bindings:
```
[BTreeMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/collections/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html)<[Action](https://docs.rs/enum.Action.html), [KeyboardShortcut](https://docs.rs/egui/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/egui/data/input/struct.KeyboardShortcut.html)>,
}## Expand description

`Action → KeyboardShortcut`. Serialisable (KeyboardShortcut is serde in egui),
so a host can save/load a remapped keymap (KEY-6). Uses `Modifiers::COMMAND`
which egui maps to ⌘ on macOS / Ctrl elsewhere (KEY-3).

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.bindings)

`bindings: `[BTreeMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/collections/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html)<[Action](https://docs.rs/enum.Action.html), [KeyboardShortcut](https://docs.rs/egui/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/egui/data/input/struct.KeyboardShortcut.html)>## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Windows preset: Ctrl-based, `Ctrl+Home/End` doc, `Ctrl+←/→` word,
`F6`/`Shift+F6` between panes (FOC-1).

Device preset: explicit, conservative — no accidental chordless single keys for destructive actions (KEY-5). Mirrors Windows nav but keeps the arrows for movement only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_core/look/keymap.rs.html#244-246)#### pub fn [shortcut](https://docs.rs#method.shortcut)(&self, action: [Action](https://docs.rs/enum.Action.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[KeyboardShortcut](https://docs.rs/egui/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/egui/data/input/struct.KeyboardShortcut.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_core/look/keymap.rs.html#244-246)

#### pub fn [shortcut](https://docs.rs#method.shortcut)(&self, action: [Action](https://docs.rs/enum.Action.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[KeyboardShortcut](https://docs.rs/egui/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/egui/data/input/struct.KeyboardShortcut.html)>

The chord bound to `action`, if any.

# FrameSource in facett_video - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-video/0.1.10/facett_video/trait.FrameSource.html

```
pub trait FrameSource {
    // Required methods
    fn
```
[frame_count](https://docs.rs#tymethod.frame_count)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html);
[frame](https://docs.rs#tymethod.frame)(&self, i: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ColorImage](https://docs.rs/epaint/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/epaint/image/struct.ColorImage.html)>;
    // Provided method
    fn [fps](https://docs.rs#method.fps)(&self) -> [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html) { ... }
}## Expand description

A pluggable decode backend (VID-1): hands the player the current frame as an
egui [ egui::ColorImage](https://docs.rs/epaint/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/epaint/image/struct.ColorImage.html) and reports duration/position so the chrome can draw
a scrubber. Deterministic backends (image sequences) make the player testable.

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

```
pub enum ClipPayload {
    Text(
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)),
    DataColumns([Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[ArrowColumnRef](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrowColumnRef.html)>),
    Rows([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)),

A typed clipboard payload. The richest form a source can offer; a target picks
the best representation it accepts (negotiation in [`PasteTarget::paste`]).

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

TSV rows (a tabular text mirror).

### Image([ColorImage](https://docs.rs/epaint/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/epaint/image/struct.ColorImage.html))

An RGBA image (e.g. a video frame or a chart export) — M2 (CLIP-4).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Custom)

Raw custom bytes under a kind tag.

# facett-timeline 0.1.10 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/facett-timeline/0.1.10

**facett-timeline** — a **swimlane Gantt**: a wall-clock time axis with stacked,
named lanes of bars, each bar optionally split into phase **segments**. The
single Spark-defining visual facett lacked — it covers the **Jobs event
timeline** (executor lifecycle + job/stage bars), the **per-stage task event
timeline** (segmented phase bars), and the **Lakeflow run Gantt**, all from one
engine-agnostic [ TimelineModel](model::TimelineModel) (a host maps Spark's
event log / REST API onto it; this crate never learns what a "stage" is).

Two halves, exactly like the rest of facett:

- [`model`] — the pure, egui-free, serializable data shape (lanes / bars / segments + the`[t0,t1]`window) with its own offset/`state_json`tests.
- [`TimelineView`] — the [`Facet`] that paints it (time axis, lane gutter, status-coloured + phase-segmented bars, click-select, scroll-zoom) and folds the laid-out bar offsets into`state_json`so a headless driver asserts the pixels as DATA.

## FC contract

- **Serializable state**(- `state_json`,- `portable_state`/- `load_state`): the active window + per-bar- `start_frac`/- `width_frac`+ the selection.
- **[**: a robot-/CLI-addressable control surface (select a bar by its stable id, zoom the window, toggle the legend) — the same gesture the canvas click drives, so headless == live.- `Msg`] enum + [- `TimelineView::update`]
- **Render-proof**: the painter, the headless [- `layout`] helper, and- `state_json`all read bar offsets from- **one**formula ([- `TimelineModel::bar_fraction_in`]), so what a test asserts IS what paints.

---

facett — a swimlane Gantt: wall-clock time axis + stacked named lanes of segmented phase bars (the Spark jobs/stage/task event timeline), a pure TimelineModel + a TimelineView Facet

# egui_kittest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/egui_kittest/^0.34/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#egui_kittest)egui_kittest

Ui testing library for egui, based on [kittest](https://github.com/rerun-io/kittest) (an [AccessKit](https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit) based testing library).

[§](https://docs.rs#example-usage)Example usage

```
use egui::accesskit::Toggled;
use egui_kittest::{Harness, kittest::{Queryable, NodeT}};
let mut checked = false;
let app = |ui: &mut egui::Ui| {
    ui.checkbox(&mut checked, "Check me!");
};
let mut harness = Harness::new_ui(app);
let checkbox = harness.get_by_label("Check me!");
assert_eq!(checkbox.accesskit_node().toggled(), Some(Toggled::False));
checkbox.click();
harness.run();
let checkbox = harness.get_by_label("Check me!");
assert_eq!(checkbox.accesskit_node().toggled(), Some(Toggled::True));
// Shrink the window size to the smallest size possible
harness.fit_contents();
// You can even render the ui and do image snapshot tests
#[cfg(all(feature = "wgpu", feature = "snapshot"))]
harness.snapshot("readme_example");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#configuration)Configuration

You can configure test settings via a `kittest.toml` file in your workspace root.
All possible settings and their defaults:

```
# path to the snapshot directory
output_path = "tests/snapshots"
# default threshold for image comparison tests
threshold = 0.6
# default failed_pixel_count_threshold
failed_pixel_count_threshold = 0
[windows]
threshold = 0.6
failed_pixel_count_threshold = 0
[macos]
threshold = 0.6
failed_pixel_count_threshold = 0
[linux]
threshold = 0.6
failed_pixel_count_threshold = 0
```
[§](https://docs.rs#snapshot-testing)Snapshot testing

There is a snapshot testing feature. To create snapshot tests, enable the `snapshot` and `wgpu` features.
Once enabled, you can call `Harness::snapshot` to render the ui and save the image to the `tests/snapshots` directory.

To update the snapshots, run your tests with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=true`, so e.g. `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=true cargo test`.
Running with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=true` will cause the tests to succeed.
This is so that you can set `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=true` and update all tests, without `cargo test` failing on the first failing crate.

`UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=true` will only update the images of *failing* tests.
If you want to update all snapshot images, even those that are within error margins,
run with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=force`.

If you want to have multiple snapshots in the same test, it makes sense to collect the results in a `SnapshotResults`
([look here](https://github.com/emilk/egui/blob/d1fcd740ded5d69016c993a502b52e67f5d492d7/crates/egui_demo_lib/src/demo/demo_app_windows.rs#L387-L420) for an example).
This way they can all be updated at the same time.

You should add the following to your `.gitignore`:

```
**/tests/snapshots/**/*.diff.png
**/tests/snapshots/**/*.new.png
```
[§](https://docs.rs#guidelines-for-writing-snapshot-tests)Guidelines for writing snapshot tests

- Whenever **possible**prefer regular Rust tests or`insta`snapshot tests over image comparison tests because…- …compared to regular Rust tests, they can be relatively slow to run
- …they are brittle since unrelated side effects (like a change in color) can cause the test to fail
- …images take up repo space

- images should…
- …be checked in or otherwise be available (egui uses [git LFS](https://git-lfs.com/)files for this purpose)
- …depict exactly what’s tested and nothing else
- …have a low resolution to avoid growth in repo size
- …have a low comparison threshold to avoid the test passing despite unwanted differences (the default threshold should be fine for most usecases!)

- …be checked in or otherwise be available (egui uses

[§](https://docs.rs#what-to-do-when-ci--another-computer-produces-a-different-image)What to do when CI / another computer produces a different image?

The default tolerance settings should be fine for almost all gui comparison tests. However, especially when you’re using custom rendering, you may observe images difference with different setups leading to unexpected test failures.

First check whether the difference is due to a change in enabled rendering features, potentially due to difference in hardware (/software renderer) capabilities. Generally you should carefully enforcing the same set of features for all test runs, but this may happen nonetheless.

Once you validated that the differences are miniscule and hard to avoid, you can try to *carefully* adjust the comparison tolerance setting (`SnapshotOptions::threshold`, TODO([#5683](https://github.com/emilk/egui/issues/5683)): as well as number of pixels allowed to differ) for the specific test.

⚠️ **WARNING** ⚠️
Picking too high tolerances may mean that you are missing actual test failures.
It is recommended to manually verify that the tests still break under the right circumstances as expected after adjusting the tolerances.

In order to avoid image differences, it can be useful to form an understanding of how they occur in the first place.

Discrepancies can be caused by a variety of implementation details that depend on the concrete GPU, OS, rendering backend (Metal/Vulkan/DX12 etc.) or graphics driver (even between different versions of the same driver).

Common issues include:

- multi-sample anti-aliasing
- sample placement and sample resolve steps are implementation defined
- alpha-to-coverage algorithm/pattern can wary wildly between implementations

- texture filtering
- different implementations may apply different optimizations *even*for simple linear texture filtering

- different implementations may apply different optimizations
- out of bounds texture access (via `textureLoad`)- implementations are free to return indeterminate values instead of clamping

- floating point evaluation, for details see [WGSL spec § 15.7. Floating Point Evaluation](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#floating-point-evaluation). Notably:- rounding mode may be inconsistent
- floating point math “optimizations” may occur
- depending on output shading language, different arithmetic optimizations may be performed upon floating point operations even if they change the result

- floating point denormal flush
- even on modern implementations, denormal float values may be flushed to zero

- `NaN`/- `Inf`handling- whenever the result of a function should yield `NaN`/`Inf`, implementations may free to yield an indeterminate value instead

- whenever the result of a function should yield
- builtin-function function precision & error handling (trigonometric functions and others)

- [partial derivatives (dpdx/dpdx)](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#dpdx-builtin)- implementations are free to use either `dpdxFine`or`dpdxCoarse`

- implementations are free to use either
- […]

From this follow a few simple recommendations (these may or may not apply as they may impose unwanted restrictions on your rendering setup):

- avoid enabling mult-sample anti-aliasing whenever it’s not explicitly tested or needed
- do not rely on NaN, Inf and denormal float values
- consider dedicated test paths for texture sampling
- prefer explicit partial derivative functions

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

- `wgpu`
- `snapshot`
- `eframe`

(or a host toolbar) drives the view through, the same effect the canvas gestures
produce. Applied by `TimelineView::update`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [layout](https://docs.rs/fn.layout.html)
- **Pure layout**— given the plotting- `content`rect (the area right of the lane gutter, below the time axis) and the active window- `[t0,t1]`, return one- `BarLayout`- `Ui`: a test calls this directly and asserts the bar rects (offsets + widths). The painter calls the SAME fn, so the asserted rects ARE the pixels.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [model](https://docs.rs/model/index.html)
- The **engine-agnostic, normalized timeline model**— the neutral shape a host (knut / nornir viz) maps a Spark**jobs event timeline**, a**per-stage task timeline**, or a**Lakeflow run Gantt**onto, and the`TimelineView`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [BarLayout](https://docs.rs/struct.BarLayout.html)
- A laid-out bar — the exact rect the painter fills for one `Bar``layout``state_json`reports their fractions — one source of truth.
- [Timeline](https://docs.rs/struct.TimelineView.html)- View
- The **swimlane Gantt**`Facet``TimelineModel`**id**(FC-5), and an optional zoom**window**over the model’s full span.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Msg](https://docs.rs/enum.Msg.html)
- A robot-/CLI-addressable control message — the named boundary a headless driver
(or a host toolbar) drives the view through, the same effect the canvas gestures
produce. Applied by `TimelineView::update`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [layout](https://docs.rs/fn.layout.html)
- **Pure layout**— given the plotting- `content`rect (the area right of the lane gutter, below the time axis) and the active window- `[t0,t1]`, return one- `BarLayout`- `Ui`: a test calls this directly and asserts the bar rects (offsets + widths). The painter calls the SAME fn, so the asserted rects ARE the pixels.

[63](#63)
[64](#64)pub fn layout(model: &TimelineModel, t0: f64, t1: f64, content: Rect) -> Vec<BarLayout> {
[70](#70)    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(model.bar_count());
[71](#71)    for (li, lane) in model.lanes.iter().enumerate() {
[72](#72)        let row_top = content.top() + li as f32 * LANE_H;
[73](#73)        for (bi, b) in lane.bars.iter().enumerate() {
[74](#74)            let (sf, wf) = model.bar_fraction_in(b, t0, t1);
[75](#75)            let x = content.left() + sf * content.width();
[76](#76)            let w = (wf * content.width()).max(if b.duration() > 0.0 { MIN_BAR_W } else { 0.0 });
[77](#77)            let rect = Rect::from_min_size(
[78](#78)                Pos2::new(x, row_top + BAR_VPAD),
[79](#79)                Vec2::new(w, LANE_H - 2.0 * BAR_VPAD),
[80](#80)            );
[81](#81)            out.push(BarLayout { lane: li, bar: bi, id: b.id.clone(), rect, status: b.status });
[82](#82)        }
[83](#83)    }
[84](#84)    out

[120](#120)impl TimelineView {
[121](#121)    pub fn new(title: impl Into<String>, model: TimelineModel) -> Self {
[123](#123)        Self { title: title.into(), model, selected: None, window: None, show_legend: true }
[124](#124)    }
[125](#125)
[126](#126)    pub fn window(&self) -> (f64, f64) {
[128](#128)        self.window.unwrap_or((self.model.t0, self.model.t1))
[129](#129)    }
[130](#130)
[131](#131)    pub fn selected_bar(&self) -> Option<&Bar> {
[133](#133)        let id = self.selected.as_deref()?;
[134](#134)        self.model.lanes.iter().flat_map(|l| &l.bars).find(|b| b.id == id)
[135](#135)    }
[136](#136)
[137](#137)    pub fn update(&mut self, msg: Msg) -> bool {
[141](#141)        match msg {
[142](#142)            Msg::Select(id) => {
[143](#143)                let exists = self.model.lanes.iter().flat_map(|l| &l.bars).any(|b| b.id == id);
[144](#144)                if exists && self.selected.as_deref() != Some(id.as_str()) {
[145](#145)                    self.selected = Some(id);
[146](#146)                    true
[147](#147)                } else {
[148](#148)                    false
[149](#149)                }
[150](#150)            }
[151](#151)            Msg::ClearSelection => self.selected.take().is_some(),
[152](#152)            Msg::SetWindow(a, b) => {
[153](#153)                let (lo, hi) = if a <= b { (a, b) } else { (b, a) };
[154](#154)                let hi = hi.max(lo + f64::EPSILON);
[155](#155)                let next = Some((lo, hi));
[156](#156)                let changed = self.window != next;
[157](#157)                self.window = next;
[158](#158)                changed
[159](#159)            }
[160](#160)            Msg::ResetWindow => self.window.take().is_some(),
[161](#161)            Msg::ToggleLegend => {
[162](#162)                self.show_legend = !self.show_legend;
[163](#163)                true
[164](#164)            }
[165](#165)        }
[166](#166)    }
[167](#167)
[168](#168)    fn has_segments(&self) -> bool {
[170](#170)        self.model.lanes.iter().flat_map(|l| &l.bars).any(|b| !b.segments.is_empty())
[171](#171)    }
[172](#172)
[173](#173)    fn status_color(status: BarStatus, th: &facett_core::Theme) -> Color32 {
[175](#175)        match status {
[176](#176)            BarStatus::Idle => th.text_dim,
[177](#177)            BarStatus::Running => th.accent,
[178](#178)            BarStatus::Done => th.point,
[179](#179)            BarStatus::Failed => Color32::from_rgb(224, 72, 72),
[180](#180)        }
[181](#181)    }
[182](#182)
[183](#183)    fn paint_axis(&self, painter: &egui::Painter, content: Rect, axis: Rect, th: &facett_core::Theme) {
[185](#185)        let (t0, t1) = self.window();
[186](#186)        painter.rect_filled(axis, CornerRadius::ZERO, th.panel_bg);
[187](#187)        const TICKS: usize = 5;
[188](#188)        for i in 0..=TICKS {
[189](#189)            let f = i as f32 / TICKS as f32;
[190](#190)            let x = content.left() + f * content.width();
[191](#191)            let t = t0 + (t1 - t0) * f as f64;
[192](#192)            painter.line_segment(
[193](#193)                [Pos2::new(x, axis.bottom() - 4.0), Pos2::new(x, content.bottom())],
[194](#194)                Stroke::new(1.0, th.panel_stroke.linear_multiply(0.35)),
[195](#195)            );
[196](#196)            painter.text(
[197](#197)                Pos2::new(x + 2.0, axis.top() + 2.0),
[198](#198)                Align2::LEFT_TOP,
[199](#199)                format!("{t:.0}"),
[200](#200)                FontId::monospace(10.0),
[201](#201)                th.text_dim,
[202](#202)            );
[203](#203)        }
[204](#204)    }
[205](#205)}
[206](#206)
[207](#207)fn phase_color(kind: &str) -> Color32 {
[211](#211)    const RAMP: &[Color32] = &[
[213](#213)        Color32::from_rgb(120, 120, 140), Color32::from_rgb(150, 110, 200), Color32::from_rgb(90, 160, 230),  Color32::from_rgb(90, 200, 140),  Color32::from_rgb(230, 170, 70),  Color32::from_rgb(200, 130, 90),  Color32::from_rgb(160, 90, 110),  ];
[221](#221)    if let Some(i) = TASK_PHASES.iter().position(|p| *p == kind) {
[222](#222)        RAMP[i % RAMP.len()]
[223](#223)    } else {
[224](#224)        let mut h: u32 = 2166136261;
[226](#226)        for b in kind.bytes() {
[227](#227)            h = (h ^ b as u32).wrapping_mul(16777619);
[228](#228)        }
[229](#229)        Color32::from_rgb(80 + (h & 0x7f) as u8, 80 + ((h >> 8) & 0x7f) as u8, 80 + ((h >> 16) & 0x7f) as u8)
[230](#230)    }

[234](#234)    pub fn local() -> Self {
[239](#239)        let exec = Lane::new("executor-1").with_bars(vec![
[240](#240)            Bar::new("exec-1 up", 0.0, 1000.0, BarStatus::Done).with_id("exec1"),
[241](#241)        ]);
[242](#242)        let exec2 = Lane::new("executor-2").with_bars(vec![
[243](#243)            Bar::new("exec-2 up", 120.0, 1000.0, BarStatus::Running).with_id("exec2"),
[244](#244)        ]);
[245](#245)        let jobs = Lane::new("jobs").with_bars(vec![
[246](#246)            Bar::new("job 0", 20.0, 420.0, BarStatus::Done).with_id("job0"),
[247](#247)            Bar::new("job 1", 430.0, 980.0, BarStatus::Running).with_id("job1"),
[248](#248)        ]);
[249](#249)        let seg = |compute: f32, shuffle: f32| {
[251](#251)            vec![
[252](#252)                Segment::new("scheduler_delay", 0.4),
[253](#253)                Segment::new("deserialize", 0.3),
[254](#254)                Segment::new("shuffle_read", shuffle),
[255](#255)                Segment::new("compute", compute),
[256](#256)                Segment::new("shuffle_write", 0.6),
[257](#257)                Segment::new("serialize", 0.2),
[258](#258)            ]
[259](#259)        };
[260](#260)        let tasks = Lane::new("stage 7 · tasks").with_bars(vec![
[261](#261)            Bar::new("task 0", 440.0, 700.0, BarStatus::Done).with_id("t0").with_segments(seg(4.0, 1.0)),
[262](#262)            Bar::new("task 1", 445.0, 620.0, BarStatus::Done).with_id("t1").with_segments(seg(2.0, 0.5)),
[263](#263)            Bar::new("task 2", 450.0, 960.0, BarStatus::Failed).with_id("t2").with_segments(seg(9.0, 3.0)),
[265](#265)        ]);
[266](#266)        let mut model = TimelineModel::new(0.0, 1000.0).with_lane(exec).with_lane(exec2).with_lane(jobs).with_lane(tasks);
[267](#267)        model.auto_window();
[268](#268)        Self::new("timeline", model)
[269](#269)    }

[272](#272)impl TimelineView {
[273](#273)    pub fn copy_text(&self) -> Option<String> {
[277](#277)        if self.model.lanes.iter().all(|l| l.bars.is_empty()) {
[278](#278)            return None;
[279](#279)        }
[280](#280)        if let Some(b) = self.selected_bar() {
[281](#281)            return Some(format!("{}\t{}\t{}\t{}", b.label, b.status.label(), b.start, b.end));
[282](#282)        }
[283](#283)        let mut out = String::from("lane\tbar\tstatus\tstart\tend");
[284](#284)        for l in &self.model.lanes {
[285](#285)            for b in &l.bars {
[286](#286)                out.push('\n');
[287](#287)                out.push_str(&format!("{}\t{}\t{}\t{}\t{}", l.label, b.label, b.status.label(), b.start, b.end));
[288](#288)            }
[289](#289)        }
[290](#290)        Some(out)
[291](#291)    }

[320](#320)    fn ui(&mut self, ui: &mut Ui) {
[321](#321)        let th = theme(ui);
[322](#322)        let (t0, t1) = self.window();
[324](#324)        ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
[325](#325)            ui.label(egui::RichText::new(format!("⟦ {t0:.0} – {t1:.0} ⟧")).monospace().color(th.text_dim));
[326](#326)            ui.label(egui::RichText::new(format!("{} lanes · {} bars", self.model.lanes.len(), self.model.bar_count())).small().color(th.text_dim));
[327](#327)            if self.window.is_some() && ui.button("⤢ Fit").on_hover_text("Reset the time window").clicked() {
[328](#328)                self.update(Msg::ResetWindow);
[329](#329)            }
[330](#330)            if self.has_segments() {
[331](#331)                let mut leg = self.show_legend;
[332](#332)                if ui.checkbox(&mut leg, "phases").changed() {
[333](#333)                    self.update(Msg::ToggleLegend);
[334](#334)                }
[335](#335)            }
[336](#336)        });
[337](#337)        if self.has_segments() && self.show_legend {
[338](#338)            ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
[339](#339)                for p in TASK_PHASES {
[340](#340)                    ui.colored_label(phase_color(p), format!("▆ {p}"));
[341](#341)                }
[342](#342)            });
[343](#343)        }
[344](#344)        ui.separator();
[345](#345)
[346](#346)        let nlanes = self.model.lanes.len().max(1);
[348](#348)        let needed_h = AXIS_H + nlanes as f32 * LANE_H + 8.0;
[349](#349)        let avail = ui.available_size();
[350](#350)        let canvas = Vec2::new(avail.x.max(GUTTER_W + 240.0), avail.y.max(needed_h.max(180.0)));
[351](#351)        let (rect, _resp) = ui.allocate_exact_size(canvas, Sense::hover());
[352](#352)        let painter = ui.painter_at(rect);
[353](#353)        painter.rect_filled(rect, CornerRadius::ZERO, th.bg);
[354](#354)
[355](#355)        let content = Rect::from_min_max(
[356](#356)            Pos2::new(rect.left() + GUTTER_W, rect.top() + AXIS_H),
[357](#357)            Pos2::new(rect.right() - 6.0, rect.top() + AXIS_H + nlanes as f32 * LANE_H),
[358](#358)        );
[359](#359)        let axis = Rect::from_min_max(Pos2::new(rect.left() + GUTTER_W, rect.top()), Pos2::new(rect.right() - 6.0, rect.top() + AXIS_H));
[360](#360)        self.paint_axis(&painter, content, axis, &th);
[361](#361)
[362](#362)        for (li, lane) in self.model.lanes.iter().enumerate() {
[364](#364)            let y = content.top() + li as f32 * LANE_H;
[365](#365)            painter.text(Pos2::new(rect.left() + 6.0, y + LANE_H / 2.0), Align2::LEFT_CENTER, &lane.label, FontId::proportional(12.0), th.text);
[366](#366)            painter.line_segment([Pos2::new(rect.left(), y), Pos2::new(content.right(), y)], Stroke::new(0.5, th.panel_stroke.linear_multiply(0.2)));
[367](#367)        }
[368](#368)
[369](#369)        let laid = layout(&self.model, t0, t1, content);
[372](#372)        let base_id = ui.id().with("timeline-bars");
[373](#373)        let mut clicked: Option<String> = None;
[374](#374)        for bl in &laid {
[375](#375)            let bar = &self.model.lanes[bl.lane].bars[bl.bar];
[376](#376)            let is_sel = self.selected.as_deref() == Some(bl.id.as_str());
[377](#377)            let base = Self::status_color(bl.status, &th);
[378](#378)            if bar.segments.is_empty() {
[379](#379)                painter.rect_filled(bl.rect, CornerRadius::same(3), base);
[380](#380)            } else {
[381](#381)                let total = bar.segment_total().max(f32::EPSILON);
[383](#383)                let mut x = bl.rect.left();
[384](#384)                for s in &bar.segments {
[385](#385)                    let w = bl.rect.width() * (s.fraction / total);
[386](#386)                    let seg_rect = Rect::from_min_max(Pos2::new(x, bl.rect.top()), Pos2::new(x + w, bl.rect.bottom()));
[387](#387)                    painter.rect_filled(seg_rect, CornerRadius::ZERO, phase_color(&s.kind));
[388](#388)                    x += w;
[389](#389)                }
[390](#390)            }
[391](#391)            let (sw, sc) = if is_sel { (2.0, th.accent) } else { (1.0, base.linear_multiply(1.4)) };
[392](#392)            painter.rect_stroke(bl.rect, CornerRadius::same(3), Stroke::new(sw, sc), StrokeKind::Inside);
[393](#393)            if bl.rect.width() > 36.0 {
[395](#395)                painter.text(bl.rect.left_center() + Vec2::new(4.0, 0.0), Align2::LEFT_CENTER, &bar.label, FontId::proportional(10.0), th.text);
[396](#396)            }
[397](#397)            let sem = a11y::Semantics::button(format!("{} · {}", bar.label, bl.status.label())).selected(is_sel);
[398](#398)            let resp = a11y::node(ui, base_id, &bl.id, Sense::click(), bl.rect, sem);
[399](#399)            if resp.clicked() {
[400](#400)                clicked = Some(bl.id.clone());
[401](#401)            }
[402](#402)            if resp.hovered() {
[403](#403)                let dur = bar.duration();
[404](#404)                let mut tip = format!("{}\n{} · {:.0}–{:.0} ({:.0})", bar.label, bl.status.label(), bar.start, bar.end, dur);
[405](#405)                for s in &bar.segments {
[406](#406)                    tip.push_str(&format!("\n  {} {:.0}%", s.kind, 100.0 * s.fraction / bar.segment_total().max(f32::EPSILON)));
[407](#407)                }
[408](#408)                resp.on_hover_text(tip);
[409](#409)            }
[410](#410)        }
[411](#411)        if let Some(id) = clicked {
[413](#413)            if self.selected.as_deref() == Some(id.as_str()) {
[414](#414)                self.update(Msg::ClearSelection);
[415](#415)            } else {
[416](#416)                self.update(Msg::Select(id));
[417](#417)            }
[418](#418)        }
[419](#419)
[420](#420)        let hover = ui.rect_contains_pointer(content);
[422](#422)        let scroll = ui.input(|i| i.smooth_scroll_delta.y);
[423](#423)        if hover && scroll.abs() > 0.5 {
[424](#424)            let px = ui.input(|i| i.pointer.hover_pos()).unwrap_or(content.center());
[425](#425)            let f = ((px.x - content.left()) / content.width().max(1.0)).clamp(0.0, 1.0) as f64;
[426](#426)            let pivot = t0 + (t1 - t0) * f;
[427](#427)            let factor = if scroll > 0.0 { 0.85 } else { 1.0 / 0.85 };
[428](#428)            let span = (t1 - t0).max(f64::EPSILON) * factor;
[429](#429)            let model_span = (self.model.t1 - self.model.t0).max(f64::EPSILON);
[430](#430)            let span = span.min(model_span); let na = (pivot - f * span).max(self.model.t0);
[432](#432)            let nb = na + span;
[433](#433)            self.update(Msg::SetWindow(na, nb));
[434](#434)            ui.ctx().request_repaint();
[435](#435)        }
[436](#436)
[437](#437)        if let Some(b) = self.selected_bar() {
[439](#439)            ui.separator();
[440](#440)            ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
[441](#441)                ui.strong(&b.label);
[442](#442)                ui.colored_label(Self::status_color(b.status, &th), b.status.label());
[443](#443)                ui.label(egui::RichText::new(format!("{:.0}–{:.0}  ({:.0})", b.start, b.end, b.duration())).monospace().color(th.text_dim));
[444](#444)            });
[445](#445)        }
[446](#446)
[447](#447)        #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[449](#449)        facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[450](#450)            "facett-timeline::TimelineView::ui",
[451](#451)            "ui_render",
[452](#452)            !self.model.is_empty(),
[453](#453)            &format!("lanes={} bars={}", self.model.lanes.len(), self.model.bar_count()),
[454](#454)        );
[455](#455)    }

[457](#457)    fn state_json(&self) -> serde_json::Value {
[458](#458)        let (t0, t1) = self.window();
[459](#459)        let mut base = self.model.state_json_windowed(t0, t1);
[460](#460)        if let Some(obj) = base.as_object_mut() {
[461](#461)            obj.insert("title".into(), serde_json::json!(self.title));
[462](#462)            obj.insert("selected".into(), serde_json::json!(self.selected));
[463](#463)            obj.insert("zoomed".into(), serde_json::json!(self.window.is_some()));
[464](#464)            obj.insert("show_legend".into(), serde_json::json!(self.show_legend));
[465](#465)            obj.insert("has_segments".into(), serde_json::json!(self.has_segments()));
[466](#466)        }
[467](#467)        base
[468](#468)    }

[491](#491)    fn load_state(&mut self, state: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
[492](#492)        let mut changed = false;
[493](#493)        if let Some(sel) = state.get("selected") {
[494](#494)            self.selected = sel.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string());
[495](#495)            changed = true;
[496](#496)        }
[497](#497)        if let Some(w) = state.get("window") {
[498](#498)            self.window = w.as_array().and_then(|a| Some((a.first()?.as_f64()?, a.get(1)?.as_f64()?)));
[499](#499)            changed = true;
[500](#500)        }
[501](#501)        if let Some(b) = state.get("show_legend").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()) {
[502](#502)            self.show_legend = b;
[503](#503)            changed = true;
[504](#504)        }
[505](#505)        changed
[506](#506)    }

`t` sits (clamped). Lets the view render against a **zoom** window narrower
than the model’s own `[t0,t1]` while reusing one offset formula.

# facett_timeline::model - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-timeline/0.1.10/facett_timeline/model/index.html

## Expand description

The **engine-agnostic, normalized timeline model** — the neutral shape a host
(knut / nornir viz) maps a Spark **jobs event timeline**, a **per-stage task
timeline**, or a **Lakeflow run Gantt** onto, and the
[ TimelineView](https://docs.rs/struct.TimelineView.html) renders. Pure + egui-free: inject lanes
and bars, assert the laid-out fractions, no painter required.

[§](https://docs.rs#shape-mirrors-the-facett-pipeline-adapter-seam)Shape (mirrors the `facett-pipeline` adapter seam)

```
TimelineModel { lanes, t0, t1 }     // wall-clock window
Lane  { label, bars }               // e.g. "executor-3", "stage 7"
Bar   { id, label, start, end,      // positioned by wall-clock time
        status, segments }          // optional intra-bar phases
Segment { kind, fraction }          // scheduler-delay / compute / shuffle …
```
Nothing here depends on Spark: the model speaks `String` labels, `f64`
wall-clock values, a neutral [ BarStatus](https://docs.rs/enum.BarStatus.html), and an open

[phase bag. The host adapter is the only place that knows what a “stage” is.](https://docs.rs/struct.Segment.html)

`Segment`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bar](https://docs.rs/struct.Bar.html)
- One **bar**on a lane: positioned + sized by the wall-clock window`[start,end]`, optionally split into`Segment`
- [Lane](https://docs.rs/struct.Lane.html)
- A named **swimlane**holding a row of bars (an executor’s lifecycle, a stage’s tasks, a job track…).
- [Segment](https://docs.rs/struct.Segment.html)
- An intra-bar **phase segment**— a fraction of the bar’s width, coloured by its`kind`. The fractions of a bar’s segments are interpreted in order; they need not sum to exactly 1 (the view normalises by their sum), so a host can hand raw per-phase millis as fractions.
- [Timeline](https://docs.rs/struct.TimelineModel.html)- Model
- The whole **timeline**: stacked lanes over a shared wall-clock window`[t0,t1]`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [BarStatus](https://docs.rs/enum.BarStatus.html)
- Neutral run status of a single bar (a job / stage / task / run). The host maps
its engine status onto this; the view maps it onto a `Theme``facett-pipeline`’s`StageStatus`, kept local so this crate needs no pipeline dependency.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [TASK_](https://docs.rs/constant.TASK_PHASES.html)- PHASES
- The canonical Spark **task-phase**order (the`TIMELINE_LEGEND`of`StagePage.scala`): where a task’s wall-clock time actually goes. A host fills a`Bar``segments``kind`s (or any free string); the view colours known phases from a stable per-phase ramp and hashes the rest.

---

### impl [TimelineView](https://docs.rs/struct.TimelineView.html)

A self-contained **demo timeline** with no host: an executor-lifecycle lane,
two job bars, and a stage’s task lane whose bars are split into the canonical
Spark task phases — exercises both timeline kinds (plain + segmented) in one
model. Used by the gallery + the render tests.

}## Expand description

The facett **component contract**. Every facet — graph, map, pipeline, table,
the ported nornir viewers — implements this, so consumers (korp, nornir, …)
compose them uniformly *and* get headless robot-testing for free.

The three things a component owes its host:

- a **title**(tab label / panel heading),
- how to **draw**itself into egui,
- its **observable state**as JSON — dumped to`$APP_STATE`for headless assertions.**Rule:**every visible list/status/count goes in`state_json`.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

Set the uniform scale; clamp internally. Default no-op (not scalable).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_core/lib.rs.html#228-230)#### fn [selection_json](https://docs.rs#method.selection_json)(&self) -> [Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_core/lib.rs.html#228-230)

#### fn [selection_json](https://docs.rs#method.selection_json)(&self) -> [Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)

The current selection as JSON (also folded into `state_json` by
convention). `Null` when nothing/none selectable.

Clipboard hooks — see clipboard.rs. Defaults: nothing to give/take. Returns the text to place on the clipboard (None = nothing copyable now).

Like `copy`, but also removes the selection. Default delegates to `copy`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_core/lib.rs.html#251-253)#### fn [as_any_mut](https://docs.rs#method.as_any_mut)(&mut self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&mut dyn [Any](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/any/trait.Any.html)>

#### fn [as_any_mut](https://docs.rs#method.as_any_mut)(&mut self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&mut dyn [Any](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/any/trait.Any.html)>

Optional downcast handle for hosts that need typed access to a specific
facet living inside a [ FacetDeck](https://docs.rs/struct.FacetDeck.html) (e.g. a robot-UI driver clicking an
app-level control that must forward to a concrete component’s own API).
Defaulted to

`None` so no existing facet has to change; a component opts in
by returning `Some(self)`.Stable component-type id (e.g. `"jobview"`, `"graphpan"`, `"table"`). Two
instances with the **same** kind can exchange portable state; the empty
default `""` means **opted out** of cross-instance clone.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_core/lib.rs.html#275-277)#### fn [portable_state](https://docs.rs#method.portable_state)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_core/lib.rs.html#275-277)

#### fn [portable_state](https://docs.rs#method.portable_state)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)>

The **portable** subset of this facet’s state — the fields a same-kind
sibling can adopt. `None` = not cloneable. Kept SEPARATE from
[ state_json](https://docs.rs/trait.Facet.html#tymethod.state_json) (the introspection dump, which may carry
derived / render-only data) so this stays round-trippable through

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.Facet.html#method.load_state)

# Msg in facett_timeline - Rust

A robot-/CLI-addressable control message — the named boundary a headless driver

produce. Applied by [ TimelineView::update](https://docs.rs/struct.TimelineView.html#method.update).

# layout in facett_timeline - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-timeline/0.1.10/facett_timeline/fn.layout.html

## Expand description

**Pure layout** — given the plotting `content` rect (the area right of the lane
gutter, below the time axis) and the active window `[t0,t1]`, return one
[ BarLayout](https://docs.rs/struct.BarLayout.html) per bar. No painter, no

`Ui`: a test calls this directly and
asserts the bar rects (offsets + widths). The painter calls the SAME fn, so the
asserted rects ARE the pixels.

---

`id: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Stable identity (selection is keyed on this, FC-5 — not a list index).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.label)

`label: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Display label (shown in/over the bar + the hover tooltip).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.start)

`start: `[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)Wall-clock start.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.end)

`end: `[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)Wall-clock end (clamped to `>= start`).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.status)

`status: `[BarStatus](https://docs.rs/enum.BarStatus.html)Run status → bar colour.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.segments)

`segments: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Segment](https://docs.rs/struct.Segment.html)>Optional intra-bar phase segments (empty = a solid status-coloured bar).

# BarStatus in facett_timeline::model - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-timeline/0.1.10/facett_timeline/model/enum.BarStatus.html

```
pub enum BarStatus {
    Idle,
    Running,
    Done,
    Failed,
}
```
## Expand description

Neutral run status of a single bar (a job / stage / task / run). The host maps
its engine status onto this; the view maps it onto a [ Theme](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/theme/struct.Theme.html)
colour. Identical in spirit to

`facett-pipeline`’s `StageStatus`, kept local so
this crate needs no pipeline dependency.## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

# facett-table 0.1.10 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/facett-table/0.1.10

**facett-table** — a generic **data-table** viewer: named columns + string
rows in a striped grid, with cell truncation + a row scroll. Generalised from
nornir's warehouse table ("oslo") — but source-agnostic (any `Vec<String>`
rows). A [`Facet`]; the consumer formats its cells to strings.

---

                    facett-table 0.1.10

                facett — generic data-table viewer (columns + string rows, striped grid)

# facett_table - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/facett-table/0.1.10/target-redirect/facett_table/

## Expand description

**facett-table** — a generic **data-table** viewer: named columns + string
rows in a striped grid, with cell truncation + a row scroll. Generalised from
nornir’s warehouse table (“oslo”) — but source-agnostic (any `Vec<String>`
rows). A [ Facet](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/trait.Facet.html); the consumer formats its cells to strings.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use warehouse::`- [PreviewTable](https://docs.rs/warehouse/struct.PreviewTable.html);
- `pub use warehouse::`- [WarehouseTableView](https://docs.rs/warehouse/struct.WarehouseTableView.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [warehouse](https://docs.rs/warehouse/index.html)
- The **warehouse browser**Facet — a multi-table picker + grid / auto bar-chart, generalised from nornir’s`src/viz/warehouse_tab.rs`(`WarehouseBrowser`) with the Iceberg/gRPC source abstracted away. See`warehouse::WarehouseTableView`**WarehouseTableView**— a generic warehouse-style data browser: a left**table picker**, and for the selected table either a striped grid OR (when a numeric column exists) a hand-painted horizontal**bar chart**, with combo pickers for the value/label columns. Generalised from nornir’s`src/viz/warehouse_tab.rs`(`WarehouseBrowser`).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Table](https://docs.rs/struct.Table.html)
- A data table: header `columns`+`rows`(each a row of cells).

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [RowId](https://docs.rs/type.RowId.html)
- A stable, domain-level identity for a row (FC-5). When present, selection is
keyed on this string instead of the visual `row.index()`, so an insert/delete that shifts visual positions does**not**silently move the selection.

# facett_table - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-table/0.1.10/facett_table/index.html

## Expand description

**facett-table** — a generic **data-table** viewer: named columns + string
rows in a striped grid, with cell truncation + a row scroll. Generalised from
nornir’s warehouse table (“oslo”) — but source-agnostic (any `Vec<String>`
rows). A [ Facet](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/trait.Facet.html); the consumer formats its cells to strings.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use warehouse::`- [PreviewTable](https://docs.rs/warehouse/struct.PreviewTable.html);
- `pub use warehouse::`- [WarehouseTableView](https://docs.rs/warehouse/struct.WarehouseTableView.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [warehouse](https://docs.rs/warehouse/index.html)
- The **warehouse browser**Facet — a multi-table picker + grid / auto bar-chart, generalised from nornir’s`src/viz/warehouse_tab.rs`(`WarehouseBrowser`) with the Iceberg/gRPC source abstracted away. See`warehouse::WarehouseTableView`**WarehouseTableView**— a generic warehouse-style data browser: a left**table picker**, and for the selected table either a striped grid OR (when a numeric column exists) a hand-painted horizontal**bar chart**, with combo pickers for the value/label columns. Generalised from nornir’s`src/viz/warehouse_tab.rs`(`WarehouseBrowser`).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Table](https://docs.rs/struct.Table.html)
- A data table: header `columns`+`rows`(each a row of cells).

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [RowId](https://docs.rs/type.RowId.html)
- A stable, domain-level identity for a row (FC-5). When present, selection is
keyed on this string instead of the visual `row.index()`, so an insert/delete that shifts visual positions does**not**silently move the selection.

[48](#48)    pub fn new(title: impl Into<String>, columns: Vec<String>) -> Self {
[49](#49)        Self {
[50](#50)            title: title.into(),
[51](#51)            columns,
[52](#52)            rows: Vec::new(),
[53](#53)            selected: BTreeSet::new(),
[54](#54)            row_ids: Vec::new(),
[55](#55)            scale: 1.0,
[56](#56)            hover_fades: FadeTrack::default(),
[57](#57)            sel_fades: FadeTrack::default(),
[58](#58)        }
[59](#59)    }
[60](#60)    pub fn push_row(&mut self, row: Vec<String>) {
[61](#61)        self.rows.push(row);
[62](#62)    }
[63](#63)
[64](#64)    pub fn with_row_ids(mut self, ids: Vec<RowId>) -> Self {
[69](#69)        self.row_ids = ids;
[70](#70)        self
[71](#71)    }
[72](#72)
[73](#73)    fn row_identity(&self, i: usize) -> String {
[77](#77)        self.row_ids.get(i).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| i.to_string())
[78](#78)    }
[79](#79)
[80](#80)    fn row_label(&self, i: usize) -> String {
[85](#85)        format!("row: {}", self.row_identity(i))
[86](#86)    }
[87](#87)
[88](#88)    pub fn select_row(&mut self, i: usize) {
[90](#90)        if i < self.rows.len() && !self.selected.insert(i) {
[91](#91)            self.selected.remove(&i);
[92](#92)        }
[93](#93)    }
[94](#94)    pub fn clear_selection(&mut self) {
[96](#96)        self.selected.clear();
[97](#97)    }
[98](#98)    pub fn selected_rows(&self) -> Vec<usize> {
[100](#100)        self.selected.iter().copied().collect()
[101](#101)    }
[102](#102)
[103](#103)    fn copy_indices(&self) -> Vec<usize> {
[105](#105)        if self.selected.is_empty() {
[106](#106)            (0..self.rows.len()).collect()
[107](#107)        } else {
[108](#108)            self.selected.iter().copied().filter(|&i| i < self.rows.len()).collect()
[109](#109)        }
[110](#110)    }
[111](#111)}
[112](#112)
[113](#113)fn truncate(s: &str) -> String {
[114](#114)    if s.chars().count() <= CELL_MAX {
[115](#115)        s.to_string()
[116](#116)    } else {
[117](#117)        let head: String = s.chars().take(CELL_MAX - 1).collect();
[118](#118)        format!("{head}…")
[119](#119)    }
[120](#120)}

[123](#123)    pub fn copy_tsv(&self) -> Option<String> {
[126](#126)        if self.rows.is_empty() {
[127](#127)            return None;
[128](#128)        }
[129](#129)        let idx = self.copy_indices();
[130](#130)        let rows = idx.into_iter().map(|i| self.rows[i].clone());
[131](#131)        Some(clipboard::rows_to_tsv(&self.columns, rows))
[132](#132)    }
[133](#133)}
