[145](#145)impl Facet for Table {
[146](#146)    fn title(&self) -> &str {
[147](#147)        &self.title
[148](#148)    }
[149](#149)    fn ui(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui) {
[150](#150)        use egui_extras::{Column, TableBuilder};
[151](#151)        let s = self.scale;
[152](#152)        let dt = ui.input(|i| i.stable_dt);
[153](#153)        let th = facett_core::theme(ui);
[154](#154)        ui.label(format!("{} rows × {} cols · {} selected", self.rows.len(), self.columns.len(), self.selected.len()));
[155](#155)        let ncols = self.columns.len().max(1);
[156](#156)        let mut row_hi: Vec<(u64, egui::Rect, bool, bool)> = Vec::new();
[160](#160)        let mut tb = TableBuilder::new(ui).striped(true).sense(egui::Sense::click());
[161](#161)        for _ in 0..ncols {
[162](#162)            tb = tb.column(Column::auto().at_least(60.0 * s).resizable(true));
[163](#163)        }
[164](#164)        let mut toggle: Option<usize> = None;
[165](#165)        tb.header(20.0 * s, |mut header| {
[166](#166)            for c in &self.columns {
[167](#167)                header.col(|ui| {
[168](#168)                    ui.strong(c);
[169](#169)                });
[170](#170)            }
[171](#171)        })
[172](#172)        .body(|body| {
[175](#175)            body.rows(18.0 * s, self.rows.len(), |mut row| {
[176](#176)                let i = row.index();
[177](#177)                let is_selected = self.selected.contains(&i);
[178](#178)                row.set_selected(is_selected);
[179](#179)                for cell in &self.rows[i] {
[180](#180)                    row.col(|ui| {
[181](#181)                        ui.label(truncate(cell));
[182](#182)                    });
[183](#183)                }
[184](#184)                let resp = row.response();
[185](#185)                let sem = Semantics::list_item(self.row_label(i), is_selected);
[193](#193)                resp.widget_info(|| sem.widget_info());
[194](#194)                row_hi.push((FadeTrack::key(self.row_label(i)), resp.rect, resp.hovered(), is_selected));
[197](#197)                if resp.clicked() {
[198](#198)                    toggle = Some(i);
[199](#199)                }
[200](#200)            });
[201](#201)        });
[202](#202)
[203](#203)        self.hover_fades.begin();
[208](#208)        self.sel_fades.begin();
[209](#209)        for (key, _, hovered, selected) in &row_hi {
[210](#210)            if *hovered {
[211](#211)                self.hover_fades.lit(*key);
[212](#212)            }
[213](#213)            if *selected {
[214](#214)                self.sel_fades.lit(*key);
[215](#215)            }
[216](#216)        }
[217](#217)        let a = self.hover_fades.advance(dt, ROW_FADE_SECS);
[218](#218)        let b = self.sel_fades.advance(dt, ROW_FADE_SECS);
[219](#219)        {
[220](#220)            let painter = ui.painter();
[221](#221)            for (key, rect, _, _) in &row_hi {
[222](#222)                let hf = self.hover_fades.factor(*key);
[223](#223)                let sf = self.sel_fades.factor(*key);
[224](#224)                if hf > 0.001 {
[225](#225)                    painter.rect_filled(*rect, 2.0, th.accent.linear_multiply((0.10 * hf).min(0.14)));
[226](#226)                }
[227](#227)                if sf > 0.01 {
[228](#228)                    painter.rect_stroke(
[229](#229)                        *rect,
[230](#230)                        2.0,
[231](#231)                        egui::Stroke::new(1.0, th.accent.linear_multiply(0.5 * sf)),
[232](#232)                        egui::StrokeKind::Inside,
[233](#233)                    );
[234](#234)                }
[235](#235)            }
[236](#236)        }
[237](#237)        if a || b {
[238](#238)            ui.ctx().request_repaint();
[239](#239)        }
[240](#240)
[241](#241)        if let Some(i) = toggle {
[242](#242)            self.select_row(i);
[243](#243)        }
[244](#244)
[245](#245)        #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[247](#247)        facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[248](#248)            "facett-table::Table::ui",
[249](#249)            "ui_render",
[250](#250)            self.selected.iter().all(|&i| i < self.rows.len()) && (self.rows.is_empty() || !self.columns.is_empty()),
[253](#253)            &format!("rows={} cols={} selected={}", self.rows.len(), self.columns.len(), self.selected.len()),
[254](#254)        );
[255](#255)    }
[256](#256)    fn state_json(&self) -> serde_json::Value {
[257](#257)        serde_json::json!({
[258](#258)            "columns": self.columns,
[259](#259)            "rows": self.rows.len(),
[260](#260)            "selected": self.selected_rows(),
[261](#261)            "scale": self.scale,
[262](#262)        })
[263](#263)    }
[264](#264)
[265](#265)    fn caps(&self) -> FacetCaps {
[266](#266)        FacetCaps::NONE.selectable().copyable().searchable().scalable().resizable().themeable()
[269](#269)    }
[270](#270)
[271](#271)    fn scale(&self) -> f32 {
[272](#272)        self.scale
[273](#273)    }
[274](#274)    fn set_scale(&mut self, scale: f32) {
[275](#275)        self.scale = scale.clamp(0.25, 4.0);
[276](#276)    }
[277](#277)
[278](#278)    fn selection_json(&self) -> serde_json::Value {
[279](#279)        serde_json::json!(self.selected_rows())
[280](#280)    }
[281](#281)
[282](#282)    fn copy(&mut self) -> Option<String> {
[285](#285)        self.copy_tsv()
[286](#286)    }
[287](#287)
[288](#288)    fn kind(&self) -> &'static str {
[291](#291)        "table"
[292](#292)    }
[293](#293)
[294](#294)    fn portable_state(&self) -> Option<serde_json::Value> {
[299](#299)        Some(serde_json::json!({
[300](#300)            "columns": self.columns,
[301](#301)            "selected": self.selected_rows(),
[302](#302)            "scale": self.scale,
[303](#303)        }))
[304](#304)    }
[305](#305)
[306](#306)    fn load_state(&mut self, state: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
[307](#307)        let obj = match state.as_object() {
[308](#308)            Some(o) => o,
[309](#309)            None => return false,
[310](#310)        };
[311](#311)        if let Some(cols) = obj.get("columns").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) {
[312](#312)            self.columns = cols.iter().filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string())).collect();
[313](#313)        }
[314](#314)        if let Some(sel) = obj.get("selected").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) {
[315](#315)            self.selected = sel
[318](#318)                .iter()
[319](#319)                .filter_map(|v| v.as_u64().map(|n| n as usize))
[320](#320)                .filter(|&i| i < self.rows.len())
[321](#321)                .collect();
[322](#322)        }
[323](#323)        if let Some(s) = obj.get("scale").and_then(|v| v.as_f64()) {
[324](#324)            self.set_scale(s as f32);
[325](#325)        }
[326](#326)        true
[327](#327)    }

[368](#368)    fn portable_state_round_trips_columns_selection_scale_between_instances() {
[369](#369)        let mut a = Table::new("repos", vec!["version".into(), "name".into()]);
[371](#371)        a.push_row(vec!["0.1".into(), "knut".into()]);
[372](#372)        a.push_row(vec!["0.2".into(), "korp".into()]);
[373](#373)        a.select_row(1);
[374](#374)        a.set_scale(1.5);
[375](#375)
[376](#376)        let env = clipboard::encode_component(a.kind(), &a.portable_state().unwrap());
[377](#377)        let (kind, state) = clipboard::decode_component(&env).unwrap();
[378](#378)        assert_eq!(kind, "table");
[379](#379)
[380](#380)        let mut b = repos(); assert_ne!(b.portable_state(), a.portable_state(), "differ before paste");
[383](#383)        assert!(b.load_state(&state));
[384](#384)        assert_eq!(b.portable_state(), a.portable_state(), "B mirrors A's column order/selection/scale");
[385](#385)        assert_eq!(b.columns, vec!["version".to_string(), "name".to_string()]);
[386](#386)        assert_eq!(b.selected_rows(), vec![1]);
[387](#387)        assert_eq!(b.scale(), 1.5);
[388](#388)    }

[483](#483)        assert_eq!(t.scale(), 4.0);
[484](#484)        t.set_scale(0.001);
[485](#485)        assert_eq!(t.scale(), 0.25);
[486](#486)        assert_eq!(t.state_json()["scale"], 0.25);
[487](#487)    }
[488](#488)}

# facett_table::warehouse - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-table/0.1.10/facett_table/warehouse/index.html

## Expand description

The **warehouse browser** Facet — a multi-table picker + grid / auto bar-chart,
generalised from nornir’s `src/viz/warehouse_tab.rs` (`WarehouseBrowser`) with
the Iceberg/gRPC source abstracted away. See [ warehouse::WarehouseTableView](https://docs.rs/struct.WarehouseTableView.html).

**WarehouseTableView**— a generic warehouse-style data browser: a left

**table picker**, and for the selected table either a striped grid OR (when a numeric column exists) a hand-painted horizontal

**bar chart**, with combo pickers for the value/label columns. Generalised from nornir’s

`src/viz/warehouse_tab.rs` (`WarehouseBrowser`).The nornir original couples this to an Iceberg warehouse + a `Warehouse.Scan`
gRPC; THIS is the reusable UI half — the source is just an in-memory map of
`table name → ``PreviewTable``. A host that has Iceberg/RPC builds those previews and feeds them in; this crate keeps no I/O. A canonical [`Facet`].

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Preview](https://docs.rs/struct.PreviewTable.html)- Table
- A previewed table: named `columns`+ stringified`rows`. The shape nornir’s`IcebergWarehouse::scan_preview`produces — but source-agnostic.
- [Warehouse](https://docs.rs/struct.WarehouseTableView.html)- Table - View
- A warehouse-style browser over a set of named `PreviewTable`

---

# facett-tabbar 0.1.10 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/facett-tabbar/0.1.10

**facett-tabbar** — the generic, themed **nav toolbar**: a control strip
(workspace/palette/About/live-style pickers + toggles, host-painted) plus a
two-row strip of tab headers, the active tab carrying the palette accent.
Adopted from nornir's `src/viz/facett_ui.rs` (`TabBar` / `TabItem` /
`BarControl`) — the header of that file explicitly says it "should live in
the upstream `facett` crate"; the only thing that kept it in nornir is the
egui 0.33↔0.34 skew (egui-snarl pins 0.33). facett is on egui 0.34, so this
is the re-home; nornir re-points to `facett::tabbar::TabBar` once its viz
bumps to 0.34 (still gated on egui-snarl shipping 0.34 — see the cut policy
note in the batch report).

Two surfaces:

- [`TabBar`] — the borrowed, zero-alloc widget (`&[TabItem]`+ an`active`id), the verbatim port of nornir's bar.`show()`returns the id of the newly-clicked tab;`state_json()`reports the tabs/active/split/controls.
- [`TabBarView`] — an**owning**canonical [`Facet`] (`local()`/`remote()`,`state_json()`,`caps()`) so a`FacetDeck`mounts the bar as a tab and a headless driver reads + drives the selection. It tracks its own`active`and clicking a header re-keys it (and records the click count).

---

# facett-syschart 0.1.10 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/facett-syschart/0.1.10

**facett-syschart** — a **system-map chart**: a handful of *free-positioned*
peer nodes (not a layered DAG) joined by edges, each carrying a **badge**
(a count / status number) and, when selected, an **inline expandable detail
panel**. Click a node to select it; its detail renders in a panel under the
canvas. The host owns *what* a node's detail is (a string here; richer hosts
draw their own widgets after `ui()` keyed off [`SystemChart::selected`]).

This is the piece [`facett_core::draw`]/[`facett_graph::GraphView`] don't
cover — those paint a *non-interactive* `Scene`; `DepGraphView` is a
*layered* DAG with a fixed deps/dependents drill-down. A "monitoring map" of
a few peer systems (a PKI/OIDC/Nexus triangle, a service mesh) wants
deterministic positions, a per-node badge, click-select, and a free-form
detail panel — that's [`SystemChart`].

Like every facett component it implements [`Facet`]: `title` / `ui` /
`state_json` (every node, badge, edge + the selection), so it drops into a
`FacetDeck` and is robot-testable through `facett_core::harness` — drive
[`SystemChart::select`] headlessly and assert `state_json`.

---

# eframe - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/eframe/^0.34/

## Expand description

eframe - the [ egui](https://docs.rs/egui/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/egui/index.html) framework crate

If you are planning to write an app for web or native,
and want to use [ egui](https://docs.rs/egui/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/egui/index.html) for everything, then

`eframe` is for you!To get started, see the [examples](https://github.com/emilk/egui/tree/main/examples).
To learn how to set up `eframe` for web and native, go to [https://github.com/emilk/eframe_template/](https://github.com/emilk/eframe_template/) and follow the instructions there!

In short, you implement [ App](https://docs.rs/trait.App.html) (especially

[) and then call](https://docs.rs/trait.App.html#method.update)

`App::update`[from your](https://docs.rs/fn.run_native.html)

`crate::run_native``main.rs`, and/or use `eframe::WebRunner` from your `lib.rs`.[§](https://docs.rs#compiling-for-web)Compiling for web

You need to install the `wasm32` target with `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

Build the `.wasm` using `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
and then use [ wasm-bindgen](https://github.com/rustwasm/wasm-bindgen) to generate the JavaScript glue code.

See the [ eframe_template repository](https://github.com/emilk/eframe_template/) for more.

[§](https://docs.rs#simplified-usage)Simplified usage

If your app is only for native, and you don’t need advanced features like state persistence,
then you can use the simpler function [ run_simple_native](https://docs.rs/fn.run_simple_native.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#usage-native)Usage, native:

```
use eframe::egui;
fn main() {
    let native_options = eframe::NativeOptions::default();
    eframe::run_native("My egui App", native_options, Box::new(|cc| Ok(Box::new(MyEguiApp::new(cc)))));
}
#[derive(Default)]
struct MyEguiApp {}
impl MyEguiApp {
    fn new(cc: &eframe::CreationContext<'_>) -> Self {
        // Customize egui here with cc.egui_ctx.set_fonts and cc.egui_ctx.set_global_style.
        // Restore app state using cc.storage (requires the "persistence" feature).
        // Use the cc.gl (a glow::Context) to create graphics shaders and buffers that you can use
        // for e.g. egui::PaintCallback.
        Self::default()
    }
}
impl eframe::App for MyEguiApp {
   fn ui(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, frame: &mut eframe::Frame) {
       egui::CentralPanel::default().show_inside(ui, |ui| {
           ui.heading("Hello World!");
       });
   }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#usage-web)Usage, web:

```
use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
/// Your handle to the web app from JavaScript.
#[derive(Clone)]
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub struct WebHandle {
    runner: eframe::WebRunner,
}
#[wasm_bindgen]
impl WebHandle {
    /// Installs a panic hook, then returns.
    #[expect(clippy::new_without_default)]
    #[wasm_bindgen(constructor)]
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        // Redirect [`log`] message to `console.log` and friends:
        eframe::WebLogger::init(log::LevelFilter::Debug).ok();
        Self {
            runner: eframe::WebRunner::new(),
        }
    }
    /// Call this once from JavaScript to start your app.
    #[wasm_bindgen]
    pub async fn start(&self, canvas: web_sys::HtmlCanvasElement) -> Result<(), wasm_bindgen::JsValue> {
        self.runner
            .start(
                canvas,
                eframe::WebOptions::default(),
                Box::new(|cc| Ok(Box::new(MyEguiApp::new(cc))),)
            )
            .await
    }
    // The following are optional:
    /// Shut down eframe and clean up resources.
    #[wasm_bindgen]
    pub fn destroy(&self) {
        self.runner.destroy();
    }
    /// Example on how to call into your app from JavaScript.
    #[wasm_bindgen]
    pub fn example(&self) {
        if let Some(app) = self.runner.app_mut::<MyEguiApp>() {
            app.example();
        }
    }
    /// The JavaScript can check whether or not your app has crashed:
    #[wasm_bindgen]
    pub fn has_panicked(&self) -> bool {
        self.runner.has_panicked()
    }
    #[wasm_bindgen]
    pub fn panic_message(&self) -> Option<String> {
        self.runner.panic_summary().map(|s| s.message())
    }
    #[wasm_bindgen]
    pub fn panic_callstack(&self) -> Option<String> {
        self.runner.panic_summary().map(|s| s.callstack())
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

-
`accesskit`*(enabled by default)*— Enable platform accessibility API implementations through[AccessKit](https://accesskit.dev/).
-
`android-game-activity``game-activity`backend via`egui-winit`on Android
-
`android-native-activity``native-activity`backend via`egui-winit`on Android
-
`default_fonts`*(enabled by default)*— If set, egui will use`include_bytes!`to bundle some fonts. If you plan on specifying your own fonts you may disable this feature.
-
`glow``glow``egui_glow`There is generally no need to enable both the `wgpu`and`glow`features, but if you do you can pick the renderer to use with`NativeOptions::renderer``WebOptions::renderer`.
-
`persistence`
-
`wayland`*(enabled by default)*— Enables wayland support and fixes clipboard issue.If you are compiling for Linux (or want to test on a CI system using Linux), you should enable this feature.
-
`web_screen_reader`*(enabled by default)*— Enable screen reader support (requires`ctx.options_mut(|o| o.screen_reader = true);`) on web.For other platforms, use the `accesskit`feature instead.
-
`wgpu`*(enabled by default)*— Enable`wgpu``egui-wgpu`There is generally no need to enable both the `wgpu`and`glow`features, but if you do you can pick the renderer to use with`NativeOptions::renderer``WebOptions::renderer`.Switching from `wgpu (the default)`to`glow`can significantly reduce your binary size (including the .wasm of a web app). See[https://github.com/emilk/egui/issues/5889](https://github.com/emilk/egui/issues/5889)for more details.By default, eframe will prefer WebGPU over WebGL, but you can configure this at run-time with `WebOptions::wgpu_options`.
-
`wgpu_no_default_features`*(enabled by default)*— This is exactly like the`wgpu`feature, but does NOT enable the default features of`wgpu`and`egui-wgpu`.This means that no `wgpu`backends are enabled. You will need to enable them yourself, e.g. like this:`wgpu = { version = "*", features = ["dx12", "metal", "webgl"] }`
-
`x11`*(enabled by default)*— Enables compiling for x11.
-
`__screenshot``EFRAME_SCREENSHOT_TO`and write a screenshot to that location, and then quit. This is used to generate images for examples.

[§](https://docs.rs#instrumentation)Instrumentation

This crate supports using the [profiling](https://crates.io/crates/profiling) crate for instrumentation.
You can enable features on the profiling crates in your application to add instrumentation for all
crates that support it, including egui. See the profiling crate docs for more information.

```
[dependencies]
profiling = "1.0"
[features]
profile-with-puffin = ["profiling/profile-with-puffin"]
```

# image - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/image/^0.25/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

This crate provides native rust implementations of image encoding and decoding as well as some
basic image manipulation functions. Additional documentation can currently also be found in the
[README.md file which is most easily viewed on
github](https://github.com/image-rs/image/blob/main/README.md).

There are two core problems for which this library provides solutions: a unified interface for image encodings and simple generic buffers for their content. It’s possible to use either feature without the other. The focus is on a small and stable set of common operations that can be supplemented by other specialized crates. The library also prefers safe solutions with few dependencies.

[§](https://docs.rs#high-level-api)High level API

Load images using [ ImageReader](https://docs.rs/struct.ImageReader.html):

```
use std::io::Cursor;
use image::ImageReader;
let img = ImageReader::open("myimage.png")?.decode()?;
let img2 = ImageReader::new(Cursor::new(bytes)).with_guessed_format()?.decode()?;
```
And save them using [ save](https://docs.rs/enum.DynamicImage.html#method.save) or

[methods:](https://docs.rs/enum.DynamicImage.html#method.write_to)

`write_to````
img.save("empty.jpg")?;
let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
img2.write_to(&mut Cursor::new(&mut bytes), image::ImageFormat::Png)?;
```
With default features, the crate includes support for [many common image formats](https://docs.rs/codecs/index.html#supported-formats).

[§](https://docs.rs#image-buffers)Image buffers

The two main types for storing images:

- `ImageBuffer`
- `DynamicImage`- `ImageBuffer`formats and supports conversions between them.

As well as a few more specialized options:

- `GenericImage`
- `GenericImageView`- `GenericImage`.
- `flat`

[§](https://docs.rs#low-level-encodingdecoding-api)Low level encoding/decoding API

Implementations of [ ImageEncoder](https://docs.rs/trait.ImageEncoder.html) provides low level control over encoding:

```
let encoder = JpegEncoder::new_with_quality(&mut writer, 95);
img.write_with_encoder(encoder)?;
```
While [ ImageDecoder](https://docs.rs/trait.ImageDecoder.html) and

[give access to more advanced decoding options:](https://docs.rs/trait.ImageDecoderRect.html)

`ImageDecoderRect````
let decoder = PngDecoder::new(&mut reader)?;
let icc = decoder.icc_profile();
let img = DynamicImage::from_decoder(decoder)?;
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::error::`- [ImageError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.ImageError.html);
- `pub use crate::error::`- [ImageResult](https://docs.rs/error/type.ImageResult.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [buffer](https://docs.rs/buffer/index.html)
- Iterators and other auxiliary structure for the `ImageBuffer`type.
- [codecs](https://docs.rs/codecs/index.html)
- Encoding and decoding for various image file formats.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Contains detailed error representation.
- [flat](https://docs.rs/flat/index.html)
- Image representations for ffi.
- [hooks](https://docs.rs/hooks/index.html)
- This module provides a way to register decoding hooks for image formats not directly supported by this crate.
- [imageops](https://docs.rs/imageops/index.html)
- Image Processing Functions
- [io](https://docs.rs/io/index.html)
- Deprecated io module the original io module has been renamed to `image_reader`. This is going to be internal. Input and output of images.
- [math](https://docs.rs/math/index.html)
- Mathematical helper functions and types.
- [metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata/index.html)
- Types describing image metadata

- Grayscale colors + alpha channel

- Immutable pixel iterator

- RGB colors.

- RGB colors + alpha channel

- A View into another image

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- An enumeration over supported color types and bit depths

- A Dynamic Image

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- `AnimationDecoder`trait
- [Encodable](https://docs.rs/trait.EncodableLayout.html)- Layout
- Types which are safe to treat as an immutable byte slice in a pixel layout for image encoding.

- Specialized image decoding not be supported by all formats

- The trait all encoders implement

- The pixel with an associated `ColorType`. Not all possible pixels represent one of the predefined`ColorType`s.
- [Primitive](https://docs.rs/trait.Primitive.html)
- The type of each channel in a pixel. For example, this can be `u8`,`u16`,`f32`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [guess_](https://docs.rs/fn.guess_format.html)- format
- Guess image format from memory block
- [image_](https://docs.rs/fn.image_dimensions.html)- dimensions
- Read a tuple containing the (width, height) of the image located at the specified path. This is faster than fully loading the image and then getting its dimensions.
- [load](https://docs.rs/fn.load.html)
- Create a new image from a Reader.
- [load_](https://docs.rs/fn.load_from_memory.html)- from_ - memory
- Create a new image from a byte slice
- [load_](https://docs.rs/fn.load_from_memory_with_format.html)- from_ - memory_ - with_ - format
- Create a new image from a byte slice
- [open](https://docs.rs/fn.open.html)
- Open the image located at the path specified. The image’s format is determined from the path’s file extension.
- [save_](https://docs.rs/fn.save_buffer.html)- buffer
- Saves the supplied buffer to a file at the path specified.
- [save_](https://docs.rs/fn.save_buffer_with_format.html)- buffer_ - with_ - format
- Saves the supplied buffer to a file given the path and desired format.
- [write_](https://docs.rs/fn.write_buffer_with_format.html)- buffer_ - with_ - format
- Writes the supplied buffer to a writer in the specified format.

# facett_syschart - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/facett-syschart/0.1.10/target-redirect/facett_syschart/

## Expand description

**facett-syschart** — a **system-map chart**: a handful of *free-positioned*
peer nodes (not a layered DAG) joined by edges, each carrying a **badge**
(a count / status number) and, when selected, an **inline expandable detail
panel**. Click a node to select it; its detail renders in a panel under the
canvas. The host owns *what* a node’s detail is (a string here; richer hosts
draw their own widgets after `ui()` keyed off [ SystemChart::selected](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html#method.selected)).

This is the piece [ facett_core::draw](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/fn.draw.html)/[

`facett_graph::GraphView`] don’t
cover — those paint a *non-interactive*

`Scene`; `DepGraphView` is a
*layered*DAG with a fixed deps/dependents drill-down. A “monitoring map” of a few peer systems (a PKI/OIDC/Nexus triangle, a service mesh) wants deterministic positions, a per-node badge, click-select, and a free-form detail panel — that’s

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html)

`SystemChart`Like every facett component it implements [ Facet](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/trait.Facet.html):

`title` / `ui` /
`state_json` (every node, badge, edge + the selection), so it drops into a
`FacetDeck` and is robot-testable through `facett_core::harness` — drive
[headlessly and assert](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html#method.select)

`SystemChart::select``state_json`.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [SysEdge](https://docs.rs/struct.SysEdge.html)
- An undirected link between two node ids.
- [SysNode](https://docs.rs/struct.SysNode.html)
- One system in the map. Positions are **normalized**(`0.0..=1.0`of the canvas), so the layout is resolution-independent and deterministic — ideal for headless rendering and screenshots.
- [System](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html)- Chart
- The system-map chart: nodes + edges + the current selection.

---

# facett_syschart - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-syschart/0.1.10/facett_syschart/index.html

## Expand description

**facett-syschart** — a **system-map chart**: a handful of *free-positioned*
peer nodes (not a layered DAG) joined by edges, each carrying a **badge**
(a count / status number) and, when selected, an **inline expandable detail
panel**. Click a node to select it; its detail renders in a panel under the
canvas. The host owns *what* a node’s detail is (a string here; richer hosts
draw their own widgets after `ui()` keyed off [ SystemChart::selected](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html#method.selected)).

This is the piece [ facett_core::draw](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/fn.draw.html)/[

`facett_graph::GraphView`] don’t
cover — those paint a *non-interactive*

`Scene`; `DepGraphView` is a
*layered*DAG with a fixed deps/dependents drill-down. A “monitoring map” of a few peer systems (a PKI/OIDC/Nexus triangle, a service mesh) wants deterministic positions, a per-node badge, click-select, and a free-form detail panel — that’s

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html)

`SystemChart`Like every facett component it implements [ Facet](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/trait.Facet.html):

`title` / `ui` /
`state_json` (every node, badge, edge + the selection), so it drops into a
`FacetDeck` and is robot-testable through `facett_core::harness` — drive
[headlessly and assert](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html#method.select)

`SystemChart::select``state_json`.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [SysEdge](https://docs.rs/struct.SysEdge.html)
- An undirected link between two node ids.
- [SysNode](https://docs.rs/struct.SysNode.html)
- One system in the map. Positions are **normalized**(`0.0..=1.0`of the canvas), so the layout is resolution-independent and deterministic — ideal for headless rendering and screenshots.
- [System](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html)- Chart
- The system-map chart: nodes + edges + the current selection.

---

[138](#138)    pub fn node_center(&self, i: usize, rect: Rect) -> Pos2 {
[146](#146)        self.center(i, rect)
[147](#147)    }
[148](#148)    pub const NODE_R: f32 = NODE_R;
[151](#151)
[152](#152)    fn center(&self, i: usize, rect: Rect) -> Pos2 {
[154](#154)        let (nx, ny) = self.nodes[i].pos;
[155](#155)        let pad = NODE_R + 6.0;
[156](#156)        let inner = Rect::from_min_max(
[157](#157)            rect.min + vec2(pad, pad),
[158](#158)            rect.max - vec2(pad, pad),
[159](#159)        );
[160](#160)        Pos2::new(
[161](#161)            inner.min.x + nx.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * inner.width().max(1.0),
[162](#162)            inner.min.y + ny.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * inner.height().max(1.0),
[163](#163)        )
[164](#164)    }
[165](#165)}
[166](#166)
[167](#167)impl SystemChart {
[168](#168)    pub fn copy_text(&self) -> Option<String> {
[172](#172)        if self.nodes.is_empty() {
[173](#173)            return None;
[174](#174)        }
[175](#175)        if let Some(n) = self.selected().and_then(|id| self.nodes.iter().find(|n| n.id == id)) {
[176](#176)            let mut s = format!("{} (badge {})", n.label, n.badge);
[177](#177)            if !n.detail.is_empty() {
[178](#178)                s.push('\n');
[179](#179)                s.push_str(&n.detail);
[180](#180)            }
[181](#181)            return Some(s);
[182](#182)        }
[183](#183)        let mut out = String::from("id\tlabel\tbadge");
[184](#184)        for n in &self.nodes {
[185](#185)            out.push('\n');
[186](#186)            out.push_str(&format!("{}\t{}\t{}", n.id, n.label, n.badge));
[187](#187)        }
[188](#188)        Some(out)
[189](#189)    }
[190](#190)}

[204](#204)    fn title(&self) -> &str {
[205](#205)        &self.title
[206](#206)    }

[208](#208)    fn copy(&mut self) -> Option<String> {
[209](#209)        self.copy_payload().map(|p| p.as_text())
[210](#210)    }
[211](#211)
[212](#212)    fn ui(&mut self, ui: &mut Ui) {
[213](#213)        let th = theme(ui);
[214](#214)        let canvas = vec2(ui.available_width(), self.canvas_h.min(ui.available_height().max(self.canvas_h)));
[216](#216)        let (rect, _resp) = ui.allocate_exact_size(canvas, Sense::hover());
[217](#217)        let base = ui.id().with("syschart-node");
[218](#218)        let painter = ui.painter_at(rect);
[219](#219)
[220](#220)        let centers: Vec<Pos2> = (0..self.nodes.len()).map(|i| self.center(i, rect)).collect();
[221](#221)
[222](#222)        for e in &self.edges {
[224](#224)            if let (Some(ai), Some(bi)) = (self.index_of(&e.a), self.index_of(&e.b)) {
[225](#225)                painter.line_segment([centers[ai], centers[bi]], Stroke::new(1.5, th.edge));
[226](#226)            }
[227](#227)        }
[228](#228)
[229](#229)        let sel_id = self.selected.clone();
[233](#233)        let mut toggle: Option<String> = None;
[234](#234)        for (i, node) in self.nodes.iter().enumerate() {
[235](#235)            let c = centers[i];
[236](#236)            let selected = sel_id.as_deref() == Some(node.id.as_str());
[237](#237)            let r = if selected { NODE_R + 3.0 } else { NODE_R };
[238](#238)            facett_core::look::elevation_shadow(ui, Rect::from_center_size(c, vec2(2.0 * r, 2.0 * r)), r);
[242](#242)            painter.circle_filled(c, r, node.color);
[243](#243)            let ring = if selected { th.accent } else { th.node_stroke };
[244](#244)            painter.circle_stroke(c, r, Stroke::new(if selected { 2.5 } else { 1.0 }, ring));
[245](#245)            painter.text(c, Align2::CENTER_CENTER, node.badge.to_string(), FontId::proportional(11.0), th.text);
[247](#247)            painter.text(
[249](#249)                c + vec2(0.0, r + 2.0),
[250](#250)                Align2::CENTER_TOP,
[251](#251)                &node.label,
[252](#252)                FontId::proportional(11.0),
[253](#253)                th.text,
[254](#254)            );
[255](#255)
[256](#256)            let node_rect = Rect::from_center_size(c, vec2(2.0 * r, 2.0 * r));
[259](#259)            facett_core::look::reveal_on_hover(ui, node_rect, r);
[264](#264)            facett_core::look::apply_focus_ring(ui, node_rect, selected, r);
[265](#265)            let label = format!("{} · {} events", node.label, node.badge);
[266](#266)            let hit = a11y_node(
[267](#267)                ui,
[268](#268)                base,
[269](#269)                &node.id,
[270](#270)                Sense::click(),
[271](#271)                node_rect,
[272](#272)                Semantics::button(label).value(node.badge as f64).selected(selected),
[273](#273)            );
[274](#274)            if hit.clicked() {
[275](#275)                toggle = Some(node.id.clone());
[276](#276)            }
[277](#277)        }
[278](#278)
[279](#279)        if let Some(id) = toggle {
[281](#281)            self.select(&id);
[282](#282)        }
[283](#283)
[284](#284)        ui.separator();
[286](#286)        match self.selected_idx() {
[287](#287)            None => {
[288](#288)                ui.weak("Click a node to expand its detail.");
[289](#289)            }
[290](#290)            Some(i) => {
[291](#291)                let node = &self.nodes[i];
[292](#292)                ui.horizontal(|ui| {
[293](#293)                    ui.strong(&node.label);
[294](#294)                    ui.weak(format!("· {} events", node.badge));
[295](#295)                });
[296](#296)                if node.detail.is_empty() {
[297](#297)                    ui.weak("(no detail)");
[298](#298)                } else {
[299](#299)                    for line in node.detail.lines() {
[300](#300)                        ui.monospace(line);
[301](#301)                    }
[302](#302)                }
[303](#303)            }
[304](#304)        }
[305](#305)
[306](#306)        #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[308](#308)        facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[309](#309)            "facett-syschart::SystemChart::ui",
[310](#310)            "ui_render",
[311](#311)            !self.nodes.is_empty(),
[312](#312)            &format!("nodes={} edges={}", self.nodes.len(), self.edges.len()),
[313](#313)        );
[314](#314)    }
[315](#315)
[316](#316)    fn state_json(&self) -> serde_json::Value {
[317](#317)        serde_json::json!({
[318](#318)            "nodes": self.nodes.iter().map(|n| serde_json::json!({
[319](#319)                "id": n.id,
[320](#320)                "label": n.label,
[321](#321)                "badge": n.badge,
[322](#322)                "pos": [n.pos.0, n.pos.1],
[323](#323)                "has_detail": !n.detail.is_empty(),
[324](#324)            })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
[325](#325)            "edges": self.edges.iter().map(|e| serde_json::json!([e.a, e.b])).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
[326](#326)            "selected": self.selected(),
[327](#327)        })
[328](#328)    }
[329](#329)
[330](#330)    fn selection_json(&self) -> serde_json::Value {
[331](#331)        match self.selected() {
[332](#332)            Some(id) => serde_json::json!(id),
[333](#333)            None => serde_json::Value::Null,
[334](#334)        }
[335](#335)    }
[336](#336)
[337](#337)    fn caps(&self) -> FacetCaps {
[340](#340)        FacetCaps::NONE.themeable().resizable().selectable().copyable()
[341](#341)    }

[354](#354)    #[test]
[355](#355)    fn typed_copy_is_selected_node_or_node_list_rows() {
[356](#356)        use facett_core::clip::{ClipKind, CopySource};
[357](#357)        let mut c = SystemChart::new(
[358](#358)            "sys",
[359](#359)            vec![
[360](#360)                SysNode::new("pki", "PKI", Color32::WHITE, (0.1, 0.1)).badge(3),
[361](#361)                SysNode::new("oidc", "OIDC", Color32::WHITE, (0.9, 0.1)).badge(7),
[362](#362)            ],
[363](#363)            vec![SysEdge::new("pki", "oidc")],
[364](#364)        );
[365](#365)        let p = c.copy_payload().unwrap();
[367](#367)        assert_eq!(p.kind(), ClipKind::Text);
[368](#368)        assert!(p.as_text().starts_with("id\tlabel\tbadge"), "{}", p.as_text());
[369](#369)        assert!(p.as_text().contains("\npki\tPKI\t3"));
[370](#370)        c.select("oidc");
[372](#372)        assert_eq!(c.copy_payload().unwrap().as_text(), "OIDC (badge 7)");
[373](#373)        assert!(SystemChart::new("empty", vec![], vec![]).copy_payload().is_none());
[374](#374)    }

[381](#381)            SysNode::new("pki", "PKI", Color32::from_rgb(120, 200, 255), (0.1, 0.1)).badge(3).detail("issued: a\nissued: b"),
[382](#382)            SysNode::new("oidc", "OIDC", Color32::from_rgb(200, 160, 255), (0.9, 0.1)).badge(7),
[383](#383)            SysNode::new("nexus", "Nexus", Color32::from_rgb(160, 255, 180), (0.5, 0.9)).badge(0),
[384](#384)        ];
[385](#385)        let edges = vec![
[386](#386)            SysEdge::new("pki", "oidc"),
[387](#387)            SysEdge::new("pki", "nexus"),
[388](#388)            SysEdge::new("oidc", "nexus"),
[389](#389)        ];
[390](#390)        SystemChart::new("System Map", nodes, edges)
[391](#391)    }

The system-map chart: nodes + edges + the current selection.

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-SystemChart)

### impl [SystemChart](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html)

The node radius (px) the free-position layout pads the canvas by, exposed so
the matrix can assert nodes land inside `rect` by exactly this inset.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_syschart/lib.rs.html#88-90)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_syschart/lib.rs.html#91-94)

#### pub fn [with_canvas_height](https://docs.rs#method.with_canvas_height)(self, h: [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html)) -> Self

Select a node by id (headless-test + host entry point). Selecting the already-selected node deselects it. Unknown id is a no-op.

Update a node’s badge by id (e.g. a live event count). No-op if unknown.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_syschart/lib.rs.html#145-147)#### pub fn [node_center](https://docs.rs#method.node_center)(&self, i: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), rect: [Rect](https://docs.rs/emath/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/emath/rect/struct.Rect.html)) -> [Pos2](https://docs.rs/emath/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/emath/pos2/struct.Pos2.html)

#### pub fn [node_center](https://docs.rs#method.node_center)(&self, i: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), rect: [Rect](https://docs.rs/emath/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/emath/rect/struct.Rect.html)) -> [Pos2](https://docs.rs/emath/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/emath/pos2/struct.Pos2.html)

**Test/host hook (additive).** The public, return-asserted view of the
private [ center](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html#method.center) layout node — the absolute pixel centre
node

`i`’s circle is painted at inside `rect`. Exposed so the syschart
call-chain matrix can assert the *layout/place*stage (finite, confined to the padded inner rect, monotone in the normalized pos) without a painter. Calls the

**same**private fn

`ui` paints with — additive, no behaviour
change. The node radius the layout pads for is [.](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html#associatedconstant.NODE_R)

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/fn.draw.html

## Expand description

Draw a `Scene` into `ui` — the reusable render primitive. Empty scenes show
`empty_hint`. Labels render when the node count is small enough to read.

# SysNode in facett_syschart - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-syschart/0.1.10/facett_syschart/struct.SysNode.html

```
pub struct SysNode {
    pub id:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub label: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub color: [Color32](https://docs.rs/ecolor/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ecolor/color32/struct.Color32.html),
    pub badge: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html),
    pub pos: ([f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html), [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html)),
    pub detail: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
}## Expand description

One system in the map. Positions are **normalized** (`0.0..=1.0` of the
canvas), so the layout is resolution-independent and deterministic — ideal
for headless rendering and screenshots.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.id)

`id: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Stable id (used for selection + edges). Unique within a chart.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.label)

`label: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Human label drawn next to the node.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.color)

`color: `[Color32](https://docs.rs/ecolor/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ecolor/color32/struct.Color32.html)Node colour (the host picks the policy — by status, by hash, …).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.badge)

`badge: `[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)A small count/status badge drawn on the node (e.g. an event count).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.pos)

`pos: (`[f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html), [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html))Normalized position in the canvas (`0,0` = top-left, `1,1` = bottom-right).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.detail)

`detail: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Free-form detail shown in the inline panel when this node is selected.
Hosts that draw richer detail can leave this empty and render their own
widgets after `ui()` keyed off [ SystemChart::selected](https://docs.rs/struct.SystemChart.html#method.selected).
